We had recommended the Paradisus to all our friends, especially to some close friends on their honeymoon, but this time it left much to be desired, and we made our dissatisfaction known at reception every moment. I left a copy of last year's review. It truly is a paradise. The drinks, the food, all the staff are incredibly friendly, especially at the Malva restaurant. Be sure to ask for the waiter Samuel Sosa; he'll make you feel like family.

reviews.author: Saul Castellanos (CompartirNoCuesta)
reviews.text: Terrible hotel in every way. I stayed for 15 days and during that time I noticed the hotel's poor infrastructure. Old, broken facilities, and even the pools smelled bad. I had a Reserve (VIP) wristband and they still charged me for everything, including room service. I couldn't access the Reserve area because I had a baby (but they didn't tell me that when I upgraded). They charged me an extra "government" tax upon arrival, but they wouldn't give me an invoice for it. The staff's service was awful, the food was tasteless and greasy, and they made everything conditional. First and last time I'll ever stay at that hotel. By the way, it's way too expensive for what it offers.

reviews.author: Karine Tremblay
reviews.text: The hotel is infested with cockroaches. There were even cockroaches in my room and in the lobby, which is surrounded by restaurants. The food at the evening buffet was very mediocre, the same quality as in Cuba. The pools were very dirty. There was a lack of chairs at the pool and on the beach; you have to pay $250 per day for all the empty beach or pool loungers. The photos of the rooms on the websites don't match the reality at all. It's very old and everything is broken (door handles, balcony door, etc.). A very outdated hotel that doesn't deserve its 5 stars. I had to quarantine all my belongings to avoid bringing cockroaches home. The only positive points are: the staff come to see us every 5 minutes for drinks, the beach is superb, the lobby is very nice, the coffee is good, and the evening entertainment is good.

reviews.author: Rafael Camargo
reviews.text:
The room did not match the images on the website/Internet, and the service, both on the beach and in the restaurants, was very poor. There were huge lines for check-in, check-out, the restaurant, and the poolside snack. We complained about the room and the service, and nothing was done; you're just another guest there, and they make no effort to please the guest. We went on our honeymoon, and it was disappointing. Luckily, we went to Playa del Carmen beforehand, to a hotel that saved the trip.

In my opinion, don't go to this hotel; change hotels. Go to a hotel where they value the guest and treat you as you should be treated, not just as another guest.

reviews.author: S R (Haifisch)
reviews.text: Terrible experience with this hotel. Upon checking in, I told the gentleman at the front desk my full name and told him about my reservation. He said it wasn't in the system. I asked him to let me in to check on the situation at the front desk, and he said he couldn't let me in. I'd have to sort it out over the phone or online. I told him to call someone so they could guide me to the front desk and sort it out. He left for two minutes and when he came back, he said he was sorry, but due to occupancy, no one could come to help me. Such terrible service and zero customer service. I obviously canceled and will never return to this hotel.

reviews.author: eva esteban
reviews.text:
Honestly, it was crazy to come here.
The pool is crazy, the music is super loud, unpleasant, the sunbeds are taken all day, if you go down at 8:30 in the morning, there are none left! It doesn't matter if you talk to any of the staff, no one pays attention to you. We had to go down at 7:00 to put down towels and get sunbeds... very harsh when you're on vacation (you're supposed to come to rest and enjoy yourself), but even so, when you weren't looking, you wouldn't have them anymore. I thought of complaining to a guy at the pool area, and he said, "You do the same," take whatever you want and take it from someone else... a cockfight over a damn sunbed with an umbrella! There aren't enough!!! A girl who looked like she was half in charge of the pool area, completely covered up, with white socks, white pants, a white long-sleeved shirt, a white hat that covered her neck, head, and face... horrible! She completely ignored everything. I don't understand how they have people like that working. That girl is the most unfriendly person I've ever seen. I think she's at the pool to scare away guests, and her colleagues are the same! There's one super nice person who realizes the situation and helps you, but can't do anything...
The pool is full of people, the water is boiling, people are eating everywhere, even in the water! The drinks are the same, people are holding glasses in the pool... at one point there were nacho and margarita remnants floating in the water...
If young people come and don't care about anything, it's the perfect place. If you want to relax, you have to pay for the adult pool, but the sun loungers don't have umbrellas.
In short... the pool is a disaster.
It's overcrowded, and there's no oversight over the insufficient sun loungers or the pool staff.
I have to say that the best thing by far, and I won't tire of repeating it, was the Balinese massage we got this morning. It was very expensive at €230 per person, they give you a discount, but it was so worth it... I've never had a massage like that before, incredible. I don't remember the girl's name, a very slim Filipina, but with fantastic strength and hands. My husband got one from his partner, and it was also spectacular, in a cabin for both of us at the same time.
I wish these girls were in Spain!! They are so worth it. They have power in their hands, they work magic on your back, they are polite, super friendly... I'm going to repeat it before we leave.

reviews.author: Valle
reviews.text: This old hotel with outdated facilities doesn't offer services befitting a 5-star rating, nor is it justified by its price. The service was appalling; we complained numerous times about the noise and the poor condition of the air conditioning, which made our stay extremely uncomfortable. It's a shame that a company like Meliá doesn't respond adequately. The food is not up to the standard the hotel chain offers at other locations. I will not return to this hotel and I advise against it, as the area is full of hotels.

reviews.author: Siri Potluri
reviews.text:
Whilst the hotel is aesthetically pleasing, and in a great location (beach front), I personally wouldn’t visit again.

On paper there appears to be many restaurants for food choices, however you have to book well in advance to guarantee a place. The additional paying guests who are members of the Reserve get priority at most restaurants which is frustrating given others have also paid for all inclusive.

I felt the food at the restaurants was not good. Kau was good but others were not. The Italian restaurant especially served very bland food, and I ended up leaving how it is possible to make Italian food taste so bad. The dinner buffet is poor quality. So if you cannot reserve a table at the restaurants then you end of needing to go to the very poor buffet.

Most of the food in the restaurants (except kau) was either tasteless, overcooked, very odd taste or tiny portions.

Drinks options were good but no menus provided.

Pool was lovely but guests hog the sunbeds from around 08.00- they leave their towels there the whole day meaning by about 09.00 there is not a single sunbed left to use. On the beach we looked at hiring a beach bed, but it was 250 USD which is extortionate.

You cannot use the spa facilities like the steam room or sauna unless you book an extortionately priced massage or treatment.

The gym was good for a hotel gym.

I enjoyed the ice cream and the cafe.
I enjoyed the pool once i decided to give up on sunbed and use the patch of astroturf under a tree.

I reported a watch missing, and got security involved. All I wanted to know was whether they had cameras and whether somebody had entered my room when I was away. The security team searched our whole room, including our fridge, individual underwears, all corners of our suitcase. They also tried to search my parents rooms in the same manner, even though I told them I had definitely not visited there room and not lost my watch there. They then started to search my parents personal belongings including pill boxes etc. this was highly intrusive. I understand they have a policy to follow, but they did not listen I really don’t see the need for them go through my underwear….

All in all, I still had a good time but I enjoyed Cancun for the beautiful beaches, snorkelling, historical sites. I would not stay at Paradisus Cancun again.

reviews.author: Pete Papadopoulos
reviews.text:
The resort was recently remodeled and it just reopened about a week ago. I went there with my wife and two kids. The service was terrible. It was very slow. It took forever to check in. We were only there a few nights and we were unable to book any restaurants because they were "full", but half the tables in the restaurants were not filled.

The bathroom on floor 0 is disgusting and has a foul odor that you can smell from a distance from the bathroom.

Getting bottles of water from anywhere in the resort is impossible.They are either "out" at every bar or they just don't want to give it out.

The pools are nice and clean. The kid area is good. The food and drink service is awful. It takes forever to get drinks. While seated, you cannot order any food, you have to go to the snack shack, which serves burgers, tenders, fries, etc. The food was good, BUT you have to wait for over an hour in line to get the food because they have two people working the snack shack.

The hours of the bars, restaurants are awful.

We changed our flight and left early. Don't stay here.

reviews.author: Sandra Mohan
reviews.text:
I am writing this review 4 days after returning from our stay, and after reflecting on the experience, my opinion remains the same—disappointing.

My family and I regularly travel to Mexico, so we are well-seasoned travellers and understand what to expect from resorts at this level. Unfortunately, this resort fell short in several key areas.

Service was the biggest issue throughout our stay. Room service consistently took between 1 to 2.5 hours, and the policy of charging after a limited number of orders felt unreasonable. We also travelled with friends who experienced even worse delays, waiting over 5 hours for room service on one occasion. Housekeeping was average at best, and restocking of basic items like water, coffee, and snacks was inconsistent and often overlooked.

The room itself was underwhelming. The shower drain frequently clogged, causing unpleasant odors, and the overall space felt small and not well maintained.
Dining was mixed. The breakfast buffet was excellent, and the dinner buffet was also great. The Italian restaurant was a highlight of our stay. However, many items across other restaurants were unavailable, and vegetarian options were limited. Nighttime entertainment also did not meet expectations.

There were ongoing repairs during the day, and we encountered flooding in hallways without proper safety signage. On the fourth floor, there were severe ceiling leaks that created large puddles of water, posing a safety hazard for guests walking through the area.

Considering the premium price of this resort, this was unacceptable.
The hotel layout was confusing and made getting around inconvenient.
That said, there were some positives. The beach was well maintained with attentive beverage service, and the pools—especially the kids pool and swim-up pool—were excellent. The coffee shop and ice cream parlor were also standout features of the resort.

Tip for future guests: Poolside chairs are often taken very early (before 7:30am) with towels and then left unused, which is very frustrating—especially for families with young children who need seating. If your budget allows, consider renting a cabana (around $300). It’s covered, offers significantly better service, and includes food like lobster, shrimp skewers, fajitas, chips and dip, along with premium top-shelf drinks and consistent staff attention.

Overall, the lack of service, organization, and attention to detail significantly impacted our experience. Based on this stay, I would not recommend this resort.

reviews.author: Shaine Kumar
reviews.text:
I stayed at the Paradisus in Cancun for five days (February 1–6, 2025) with my girlfriend, family, and friends.

Positives: The beach is a highlight—spacious and enjoyable. The swim-up bar bartender was attentive and friendly, adding to the relaxed vibe. The buffet restaurant stood out as well, offering good food quality and a decent selection compared to other dining options.

Negatives: We paid for a Family Concierge Ocean View room, but upon arrival, we were assigned a bottom-floor room in Pyramid 3 with no view of the water at all. Despite complaining to the front desk, we received no resolution or assistance.

The restaurants, aside from the steakhouse, were disappointing. Service was consistently slow, and the food quality was subpar. I wouldn’t recommend booking most of the à la carte restaurants; I’d have preferred sticking to the buffet every night.

To make matters worse, on the second-to-last night, $100 CAD was stolen from our room—presumably by housekeeping. The money was in my girlfriend’s wallet, zipped inside another bag within a backpack. While it was our fault for not using the room safe, the incident was incredibly disappointing. We reported it to hotel security and staff, who promised to follow up after their investigation, but we never heard back—complete radio silence.

I won’t be returning to this property on my next visit to Cancun and will take my business elsewhere.

reviews.author: Eileen Conton
reviews.text: I’m going to start by saying the hotel is beautiful. Do i recommend it? No, i’ll tell you why… Is an expensive hotel and we received the worse service. If you did not booked the concierge experience they treat you like you are nobody, they try to force you to get the package with the concierge and once you say no the black list you. Without that package you have to make a line to make reservations on the restaurants. Once you try to make reservations for the restaurants they tell you they are all booked so you can get frustrated and upgrade your package to concierge package. They leave the restaurant reservations for those with the upgrade. The restaurants could be empty but they’ll tell you is all booked, i know because i watched all night how tables were empty and they do not accept walk ins (when you pay your money to eat good). I was able to go to one of the restaurants there and the food was disgusting. A I had to go outside the hotel every night for dinner because the hotel i payed for all inclusive did not have a table for me in any restaurant on the premises.  Overall, this place is just good for pictures, if you are trying to book a hotel with good food and experience this is not it. Do not recommend it.

reviews.author: Cameryn Porter Choate
reviews.text:
We stayed 5 nights here last week. The experience was very hit and miss. We did two days at the pool on the adults only (reserve) side of the resort in reserved Bali beds. The first day we had excellent service and were very happy! The gal waiting on us checked on us frequently. The second day we spent in the reserved Bali bed we were checked on very little, had to retrieve drinks from the bar as waiter wasn't coming around frequently, ordered lunch through the app for the same reason, and at one point the staff had congregated directly by our bed and were chatting for several minutes which was a bit awkward. During that same day a staff member was literally painting the base of the Bali bed as we were laying in it... not very comfortable!

The buffet food was just okay. Some things better than others... some staff friendlier than others as well. The restaurant experience was much better with the exception of our dinner at Cielo which was not the best. Food wasn't great and service was very slow and Cielo. Sante was fantastic for both breakfast and dinner and Sal was great as well! Cappella was great service too!

Communication wasn't great. We were told our concierge would reach out quickly after checking in to assist us with reservations. We didn't hear from him until about 2pm on our second day and many of the restaurants book out days in advance so our reservation options were limited to what was available. When we didn't hear from the concierge in a timely fashion we were able to find a reservation table with staff members to assist us.

Rooms were okay! Not super noteworthy but worked for us. Shower and tub are nice. Walls are super thin, we heard a lot from our neighbors. We did find out from one of the staff members that the hotel is closing down in May and will be closed for a year as they complete major renovations. This makes sense considering a lot of the resort was in need of some attention. The resort is beautiful and photographs nicely but could definitely benefit from some renovations. It rained one day and the inside of the resort had  towels placed everywhere I assume because of leaks in the building.

Jesus from Cappella was amazing! He recommended the tagliata di manzo al rosmarino to my husband and it was delicious! 10/10 service and great food, beverage, and atmosphere! Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Khodadad Javaheri
reviews.text:
Our stay at Paradisus Cancun was unfortunately far below what we expected from a five-star all-inclusive hotel. While there were some positives, significant issues greatly impacted our experience.

Positives:
•	Beautiful beach: The beachfront was stunning and well-maintained.
•	Large, clean pool: The pool area was enjoyable and offered a relaxing atmosphere.
•	Friendly and helpful staff: The servers and bartenders were particularly kind and attentive, enhancing the dining and bar experience.

Negatives:
1.	Maintenance Issues:
•	We experienced a ceiling leak in our bathroom that required multiple follow-ups to address.
•	When we requested a resolution, we were told we could upgrade to a renovated oceanfront room for $100 extra instead of having the problem fixed promptly. This approach felt opportunistic and inappropriate given the circumstances.
2.	Cleanliness Problems:
•	We saw small roaches 3 times: once in the restaurant on the ground, once in our hotel room on the ground, and once in the hotel room drawer where clothes were stored.
•	We also found a dying bug inside the fridge in our room, which was highly unpleasant and concerning.
•	These cleanliness issues are unacceptable for a five-star property.
3.	Outdated Rooms:
•	The rooms felt old and in need of renovation. This detracted from the overall experience.
4.	Food Quality:
•	Across all restaurants, the food was bland and uninspiring, not meeting the standards expected at this price point.
5.	Missed Room Cleaning:
•	Room cleaning was missed entirely on one day of our stay.
6.	Weak Entertainment Options:
•	The entertainment was underwhelming, with short and unengaging events. Many evenings, we found ourselves unsure of how to spend our time due to a lack of compelling activities.

Overall, while the beach, pool, and staff were lovely, these positives could not outweigh the significant shortcomings in maintenance, cleanliness, and food quality. The experience was well below five-star standards, and we would not consider returning.

reviews.author: Angelica Escobedo
reviews.text: Overpriced compared to other nearby resorts. Rooms are dated, raggedy & beds uncomfortable and leg to bed about to fall off. Common areas and restaurants are remodeled. Food is ok, drinks were good, service was great. Huge inconvenience in allowing people to reserve all the spots on the beach, they should be first come first serve. Beach and water were great,  end of Feb. Not worth going back.

reviews.author: Ronya Buzbee
reviews.text: The room was small, but clean.  Some flying bugs but I imagine the environment makes it hard to control those.  Staff was very friendly and location was in great proximity to airport.  Food was mediocre at best.  We tried all the restaurants and were not impressed at all by any of them.  The biggest issue though was with the pools. It was either 5-6ft depth or 2ft depth. This is difficult if you have a 7 year old who is not a strong swimmer but way too big for the 2ft baby pool. We always either had to be in the pool with her or had to watch her every second.  I would not recommend this resort to families with elementary aged children.  And I have a major issue with the cleanliness of the pools. Four days into our trip my daughter got hand foot mouth disease.  I am 100% sure she got it from the pool.  Main pool with the swim up bar specifically.  Always noticed things floating on top but assumed it was safe and treated with the necessary chemicals.  Not the case. You need to check your chlorine levels and sanitize.  Super grossed out by this.

reviews.author: Wealthy CM
reviews.text: We went at Paradisus through Sunwing and booked the ocean front king room but they gave us double bed room which we said we cannot have this for entire week stay. They said they only have this room for a night and can come back tomorrow to check if king bed room is available which we did and they provided a king room but with not great ocean view which was disappointing since we paid premium price for this.During our stay we felt very much racism from all of the servers and bar tenders. They were not giving any attention to what we ask and do not answer our questions. I also want to shout out to one of the bartender who was very rude and he mixed multiple alcohol in our drink when we just asked for one. This bartender was at the pool bar where there is sitting in the water at the bar. Restaurant are not that great and nobody was attending us and ignoring us more. Only white peoples are served well was noticed in our entire stay for a week so none white peoples think twice before booking. Restaurants reservations is a big scam as they only give you those that are not working with you times.

reviews.author: chiaowei yu
reviews.text:
Our experience at Paradius Cancún was far from what we expected. We paid extra for a package that included airport shuttle service, but the ordeal we went through was incredibly frustrating. Despite providing our booking information well in advance and attempting multiple follow-ups via email and phone calls (which included getting hung up on twice), we never received confirmation. Upon arrival, their shuttle company couldn’t locate our reservation and suggested we take a taxi and get reimbursed at the hotel. However, when we reached the hotel, they outright denied any reimbursement, claiming we hadn’t arranged the trip—even though we clearly had.

While the restaurant staff were pleasant, the core customer service left much to be desired. At check-in, we asked for an overview of how the hotel operates, including dining options. Shockingly, the front desk staff couldn’t provide answers. We later found out from other guests that except for the buffet, all other restaurants required reservations, which could only be made at a specific desk with unreasonably long lines every single day.

This was the worst experience I’ve ever had at an all-inclusive hotel. Guest services were not only unhelpful but downright rude. One staff member even mocked our attempts at speaking Spanish, which was both disrespectful and unprofessional.

To make matters worse, the quality of the accommodations was disappointing. Both our room and our friends’ room (who paid extra for better service) had issues. Our power went out, and our door was so poorly maintained that it let in noise all night, making it hard to sleep. The hotel itself gives off a nice impression initially, but everything feels poorly maintained, as if held together with glue.

It’s unfortunate because this hotel has potential, but the lack of upkeep.

If you’re looking for a luxurious experience with worry free services - this is not the hotel you’d want to spend your vacation at.

reviews.author: Pratibha Gaglani
reviews.text: We went over the new year break, paying higher than normal rates. Our room wasn't given to us until 3 pm! We were there an hour or so early. One of the days the rooms did not have water for several hours!!! Although the location is awesome, food is pathetic..like a 0.. booking a restaurant and finding a table was so difficult and painful. On new year eve restaurants charged 50$ per head or 90$ for the party. Anything of interest had an extra price tag. Money minting tactics. Disappointed beyond the location!!!!! Never again.

reviews.author: Info TJG
reviews.text:
Food was mid At the buffet.
Lemon fish and Sal are only upgrade restaurants I recommend with good food.  (unfortunately there was a roach in our plate.)
Location  is excellent
Lobby was excellent
Reserve manager aelissia not great.
Enrique our concierge as many others on reserve were not super helpful and was becoming difficult and argumentative when we notified of our poor experience.

reviews.author: mohit bhatia
reviews.text:
Disappointing Start to Our Stay at Paradisus Cancun

I'm writing this review after our first day at Paradisus Cancun, and unfortunately, it's been a disappointing experience so far. We arrived at the resort excited for our vacation, but the check-in process was a nightmare. The queue was incredibly long, and it took us over an hour to get checked in. This was not the welcome we were expecting.

Once we wait for our room, we were looking forward to exploring the resort and trying out the food. Unfortunately, the food was just average, and what's worse, there was no allergy information label available with food, it’s either missed or wrong label. As someone with food allergies, this was a major concern for me. It was very difficult to identify which foods were safe for me to eat, and we had to rely on the staff to provide us with information, which was not always accurate.

Overall, our first day at Paradisus Cancun has been a letdown. We're hoping that things will improve over the next few days, but for now, we're disappointed with the service and amenities.

*Rating:* 2/5 stars

*Recommendation:* If you have food allergies, be prepared to ask a lot of questions and take extra precautions. Also, consider arriving early for check-in to avoid long queues.

I hope this review helps others who may be considering staying at Paradisus Cancun.

reviews.author: Evelyn Lu
reviews.text: The beach is beautiful and the facility is nice  although you can tell it’s dated. Staff are nice to your face , however , when we arrived , we gave a big tip to our concierge , only to find out later on that she was not really our concierge and was only leading us to our room. When she greeted us, I asked point blank if she was our concierge for our stay until the end. She said yes, and that was a lie. Our real concierge still has not added me on WhatsApp , as front desk mentioned he would. So be cautious of staff not being truthful on some occasions

reviews.author: S. M.
reviews.text:
received an injury in the room and the hotel management extremely elusive when I tried to bring up a safety concern.  Eventually I was able to reach an understanding with the general customer service but it was a bit of a cat and mouse game for something that was straight forward.

I wasn't happy with the experience overall. I would stay here again. the area in general looks good. The beach is clean and amazing. would consider trying near by properties like the Marriott

reviews.author: Chuck Leisinger
reviews.text: My first all inclusive experience. Rooms were dated and worn, holes in sheets, fixtures seemed rickety. Food was plentiful and some of it was quite good but most of it was not very good. I would say there is 1-2 standout options at each themes restaurant and if I could have gotten things a la carte from each place I would have given the food a solid 4 stars. Some staff were above and beyond helpful and some were clearly so so so unhappy with their work and with tourists. Different areas of the hotel had a foul smell but some of it smelled heavily of the air fragrance. The pools closed at 7pm, way too early! The coffee station frequently out of ice, out of milk, only one person working. Never enough towels out in the pool area and the only way to get towels is to talk to the excursion hawkers. The plants and fountains inside were really nice and made for a charming atmosphere. The convenience store inside had very limited options for purchase in terms of snacks and beverages and always seemed to have issues with the point of sale system.

reviews.author: DeAndra
reviews.text:
I honestly think giving two stars is being generous. I stayed for my bachelorette trip and was extremely disappointed.
1) the room we booked through the website did NOT look like the room we were in. It was super outdated and the room on the website looked more updated. We booked the Premium Suite Sunset View.
2) there was baby roaches in the room!!
3) we got back to our A/C leaking so bad it was flooding our room by the front door. We went down stairs to let the front desk know. Came back to it still leaking. Called the front desk again letting them know it was still leaking but would be gone for dinner however we didn’t care if they entered. Came back again STILL leaking. I’m assuming a worker was waiting for us because he happen to scare us. Due to the language barrier, we really couldn’t communicate. He did tell us it’s leaking because of the a/c… as if we didn’t already know that and that management would have to fix it. Why didn’t management fix it the first time? Overall very frustrating.
4)  The other sliding door would not shut all the way, almost like it was stuck. It didnt really bother us bc we were sleeping in the other room. It ended up getting really hot in that room. We later found out if the sliding door is not shut correctly the a/c will not turn on. Yet, another broken thing in the room.
The overall resort was beautiful buy our room was giving super cheap. So i say it was waste of money, would not recommend this resort or stay again.

reviews.author: Ushasrireddy Devireddy
reviews.text:
We had an Ok experience at this resort. Resort looks beautiful with tropical vibe however the air conditioning is very poor in all the areas except your rooms.We were there in January, and this is our experience imagine the situation in Summer. Rooms are outdated and during our stay the bathroom started to look and water started dripping, however room service was responsive and addressed the issue. There was a big cockroach in the bathroom on our last day at this resort, I didnt care to complain since we were leaving anyways.

Food is a night mare at buffet, dont even attempt. Driest desserts and cold food. If you are a vegetarian, except for salad, some potatoes there is nothing much.Food is better in the restaurants but you need to reserve them for dinner and only two are open during the day for lunch. Pizza place is ok.

If you are travelling with younger kids, there is nothing for them to do except the pool.

reviews.author: Jasmine Cano
reviews.text:
I’m going to write a very honest review. I stayed at Paradisus in 2016, and I had such an amazing experience. It truly felt like a resort. Fast forward to 2024 my impression on the hotel has completely changed.
Here is my review:
- If your stay consists of any rain, then your room is at risk of water leaking into your room. My sisters room completed flooded & mine leaked with water. I had to put a bunch of towels by the window to prevent water from going everywhere.
- Hotel is old & you can see paint coming off the walls, looks like it has not been renovated in years.
- You will see towels randomly on the floor in the atrium due to water leaking inside building.
- Food is okay, nothing special. Pizza bar by the pool was good.
- Staff is nice and helpful, but only when you tip good.
- Towels have been downgraded from 2016. They are cheaply made now.
- Buffet gave me a really bad stomach bug

Overall, I would NOT stay here again.

reviews.author: Khamsang Kai
reviews.text:
We stayed here for a week and had a mixed experience. On the positive side, the food was fantastic, and the beach was beautiful—definitely the highlights of our stay.

However, there were significant issues with the room. When we checked in, we found a drill and several nails left on the sofa.On the balcony, we faced a more alarming situation: my two-year-old found a cigarette butt and put it in his mouth. Upon inspecting the area, we discovered numerous cigarette butts scattered on the floor of the balcony and deck—an obvious safety hazard for young children. We were too exhausted to request a room change after our journey.

Also there was cockroach on one of buffet section. !!!

reviews.author: Nicholas Gingras
reviews.text:
Just came back from my trip there.
Pros : Nice beach, the hotel public spaces are beautifull, staff members are very friendly and food is always available and you can always find something to eat.
Many mant activités for kids. Okay rooms, good A/C.

Cons : You will never be allowed to swim in the ocean at the resort. On a day with little to no wind flag was still red and lifeguard running after you if you go into the water. You can always go swim to neighbor resorts who were yellow most of the time.
There is not enough chairs at the pool/beach and people are fighting over it. Not sure if its on purpose, but you can rent a cabana for 250$ USD per day if you want to make sure to lay down somewhere other than the ground.
So many things at the other are only available to their elite members (somewhere to lay down at the pool, some restaurants, many meal choices at the restaurants, etc.)
We made sure when we booked to call the resort and ask if it was possible to get adjacent rooms since we were travelling with a baby and parents to make it easier. When we got there they told us it wasnt possible to put us on the same floor.

reviews.author: Milena Quintana
reviews.text: i came here for a wedding and not only did our coordinator not show up to the rehearsal but showed up late to the ceremony leaving our guests waiting for 30 minutes past the excepted time. and we payed for the “elite” wrist band or package whatever, we were denied access by the workers to the stuff we should have been granted. constant bug and leakage problem in the rooms. the chairs by the pool do not recline at all and are at a very uncomfortable angle. there is also some loud music somewhere late at night, no matter the location of your room. waited 1 hour for room service. to add, at the end of the wedding the bride and groom wanted everyone to jump in the pool next to the reception, and right as we jumped in the coordinator finally did her job and yelled at us to get out. the poolside service was pretty good, special thanks to dirdir and jose who showed excellent efficiency.

reviews.author: mariam caceres llorente
reviews.text: We had the family concierge ocean view room. We are a family of 4, bathroom doesn’t have door, the pillows smelled rotten, in general the cleaning was okay. Snack bar was poorly stocked on daily basis, in my whole one week stay shower cap was never replaced. No soap bars, gown and slippers are provided upon request that’s not what you expect from a 5 star pricy hotel. We did enjoy every o however will not recommend. The hotel is way to pricey for its quality. Also the family concierge main desk no body is ever around. Trust me at Thai resort you are not getting what you paid for.

reviews.author: vivekjs s
reviews.text:
This a review to the OTIUM desk at Paradisus Cancun resort specifically. An agent works for OTIUM called Miguel met us in swimming pool. We booked coco bongo ticket from him with the promise that he will give us coco bongo Souvenirs for the general admission  fee of $87.
He was supposed to come and give the Souvenirs next day. Even after multiple follow up s and asking other agents at thr desk, he was keep lying saying he will come and hand over. Until we left the facility he never showed up. There is no advantage of booking through them. You get the same price at the coco bongo entrance itself.

Be careful with this guy Miguel if at all you are booking any activities with him at Paradisus. We are ok even if there was no souvenirs, but the way he was keep lying about it and make us wait for him to arrive was not acceptable and unpleasant experience.

Paradisus is a great resort. No complaints about the resort. We had great time at the resort.

reviews.author: Amanda Adamic
reviews.text: I wanted to like this place, but I just hated it. There is not enough outside seating for guests and no shade. The umbrellas were few and far between. The beds and covered cabana areas they charge $250 per day, trying to hock it like the champagne is worth it. The inside is nice enough but a little maze like. Food and drinks were just okay. We were in a room directly by the smoking area and music would be played loudly during the day. There were private events with an entire pool area shut down for the day so the very limited space became even more cramped. There are nicer, larger resorts to choose for the same price. Also, you have to use an app to order room service- which is an extra charge. For an all inclusive, that should be included. Spa prices are high. Edit: The cost of sunblock is $50 and the additional costs of the restaurants that are not included are ridiculously expensive. $300 for 2 people to have steak.

reviews.author: ST
reviews.text: By far the worst "all inclusive" resort I've ever been to. WAY too few beach and pool chairs, to the point where we had to spend minimum 30 minutes hunting for chairs every day. The food is pretty bad, and I also got food poisoning (don't eat the fish if you do go here). Lots of upcharges for basics at a supposedly "all inclusive" hotel (better meals at the restaurants, better drinks at the bars, room service, etcetera). Tons of salespeople constantly trying to sell everyone crap all over the property. The bed in our room was very uncomfortable and made it hard to sleep well (and worth mentioning for reference, I normally sleep particularly well). To give them credit where it's due, the service at the beach and pool bars was good, most of the staff is very friendly, and the beach is very nice.

reviews.author: Emily
reviews.text:
My boyfriend and I went to Cancun for new year’s and had a lackluster experience at Paradisus.
TLDR: not worth the price, many inconveniences, could most likely find much better service for the same price somewhere else

We’ve never done an all inclusive but wanted to go to cancun for a relaxing trip and spend our time in the resort. We stayed for 3 nights. The staff was very friendly and spoke/understood english. However, there were many inconveniences that did not make this place worth it. The most annoying thing was the power would go out in our room periodically. At first we called the front desk and they said it was a breaker issue. However, it kept going out and for some reason we would have to open our door and then close it for the lights to come back on. Not sure what the issue was but it was definitely inconvenient. Also I know it wasn’t the lights being motion censored because the power for the outlets charging my phone would stop working as well. Secondly, you have to make all dinner reservations in person. We waited in line for an hour on our first morning to make a reservation for new year’s eve dinner. Their NYE special dinner event was $90 per person and we did not think that was worth it considering the food we had thus far wasn’t great. There was no big NYE celebration for guests unless you paid for the event. It was frustrating that we wasted an hour waiting in line for this.

My boyfriend had called ahead of our stay and booked a massage and facial for us. However when we went to the spa for our appointment, they couldn’t find it and said they were booked up for the day. They were able to get us a spot for the next day but it was inconvenient since we had planned our morning/day around the spa appointment we thought we had. The spa experience itself was nice but it was quite expensive, over $300 for the both of us for the hydra therapy (which was “free”) and a 50 min massage. The massage was nice but I’ve had better in NYC for less than $100 for an hour long treatment. On our last night we ordered room service and were told it would take 40 minutes. After over an hour our food hadn’t arrived and we had to call to make sure we would still be able to get it.

We tried to make transportation accommodations to the airport but were told it was only for guest who stayed 4+ nights, otherwise it was $85 which was quite expensive considering the drive was only 30 minutes. We ended up booking a shuttle through a separate company for $45

The only good thing about this place was the pool service and private beach. However, we had to wait 30 minutes to get towels on the first day (we went out around 12 pm). I understand we went at a busy time of year and the place was likely very booked but things like that just did not make this place worth it for the price. The next day we went out at 10 am and still weren’t able to find seats around the pool or beach. And any resort in cancun would get you the same kind of pool/beach service so it wasn’t exactly special.

reviews.author: Allie Katz
reviews.text:
I don’t typically leave reviews, but my experience of Paradisus Cancun was NO WHERE near what I hoped or expected, especially given the cost.

By no means was everything awful. The public spaces in the resort were largely quite lovely and pleasant to be in. The resort was large and didn't feel overly crowded, though around meal times the parts of the resort where most of the restaurants were could get quite busy. The spa was small but nice and the massage therapists were fantastic. It felt like certain staff members went above and beyond and some of the food was quite tasty.

But that’s kind of where the pleasantness ends. The whole resort in a lot of ways felt like a bait and switch. We bought into the premium all-inclusive package, or The Reserve, as they call it, which supposedly included access to an adult only area in the resort, premium alcohol and food, and a private concierge. The adult only area was fine, though not particularly large, and the private concierge was helpful, but even though we were lead to believe that we would have access to everything as part of the Reserve, we would discover later that premium alcohol was only included within the sectioned off parts of the resort, and that large chunks of every restaurant were an extra charge. Not just a supplemental charge, but paying full price. This felt like a huge betrayal of the all-inclusive mentality, and the constant up selling of these extra charge items felt quite inappropriate. God help you as well if you AREN’T part of the Reserve, because then they really slap you with extra charges for everything. Bali beds by the main hotel pool cost around $225 for the day. At least we got those included in our private section of the resort.

The resort itself is quite run down and in need of renovation. We had to move rooms because our first room was full of broken things, like door handles and towel racks. Our second room was better, but still had a broken toilet seat and holes in the walls where stuff used to be. You can find things in poor condition all over the resort if you look. The rooms themselves also felt sparse and plain compared to the photos where the walls were painted and the room was smartly decorated. I’ve stayed in worse rooms, but given the cost of this place, I expected a lot better than this.

Service in the resort was a mixed bag with both extreme ends of the spectrum. Some staff were incredibly helpful and attentive and seemed to want to create a nice experience, where others were very checked out, or seemed untrained and confused. The people walking around upselling excursions or asking to come listen to a 90 minute presentation selling their 'exclusive membership' (think time share but maybe worse) were also a bit much and not what you want when you're trying to relax. I feel bad because clearly some folks are trying really hard, but on the whole their effort is not enough to make up for all the short comings of this place.

There's just a pervasive cheapness to this place that feels like it goes hand in hand with all the upselling. The lack of physical menus anywhere, QR codes that lead to broken web pages or apps that barely function, and cheap plastic cups instead of glassware everywhere but the nice restaurants. Menu items would arrive missing ingredients, if they were available at all. Corners seemed to have been cut everywhere, and it's not what you should get when you're spending as much as you are to stay here.

Tldr: this place is pretty on the surface, but it’s run down and not a true all-inclusive resort in the end, instead it’s one where only half of the offerings are actually included and you’ll get pushed towards spending more money at every turn.

reviews.author: Karla W
reviews.text:
We were really looking forward to stay in this hotel but it was not what we expected.
Before checking in, we called the hotel to confirm our reservation, we got transferred to front desk but they never picked up.
My husband emailed the hotel a couple of times hoping to set up a birthday amenity since we were coming in to celebrate my birthday, they never responded. No big deal.
When we checked in, front desk people were not the friendliest. We ask if there was any ocean view upgrades available since we were there for a celebration, they could only offer a lagoon view for extra $200 per night so we opted out on that one. After checking in, we had the worst room possible. EXTREMELY outdated. We had a parking lot view. The bed was dirty, when flipping the blankets there were chunks of hair. The tub was falling apart and so on. Also, they did not replenish the mini bar for a couple of nights which we had to ask multiple times every day. We called the front desk to ask if there was an opening on any other rooms but they never picked up so we had to walk to the front desk and ask. When we got to front desk, there was no guests and they were not busy at all and just talking to each other. When my husband asked for the room, they just straight flat out said no.
This place does not care if you are there for a celebration or what. Not even a greeting when mentioned not that it mattered but it would have been appreciated at least.

Restaurants-
Buffet was not the best food.
We had upset stomach on one of the nights we stayed
Lemon fish was a long wait. We got in at 9:30pm and about 15-20mins we got our food they told us it was already last call. Sushi was awful.
BLUE AGAVE was the only restaurant that was really good. Tacos were 👌🏻👌🏻👌🏻

Drinks- almost all the drinks we ordered were watered down. Not strong at all. We liked hanging out at the bar area at Kanna Beach Club because the view from the bar was amazing but the Bartenders are not the friendliest either. Looks like they are always hassled when you order.
There was one bartender there who worked at night shift named Salvador I believe who was really nice.

Ginger bar was the bar who had a nice bartender named Christian. He made our martinis really good and down to the tee. We were impressed because he was not like the other bartenders from the other bar who just hands you a drink full of ice.

Paid ton of money to stay at this resort only to be getting mediocre service.

We loved the beach front of Paradisus though. The beach was Phenomenal!

reviews.author: Rukhsar Nadeem
reviews.text: Don’t come to this resort if you’re planning to be relaxed and enjoy your vacation. Everything here comes with some issues, and nothing is smoothly done. They call it “all inclusive” but there’s tons of things that are excluded from their so called “all inclusive” resort. For instance, the pool cabanas are only given to you for free for 2 days and after that you have to pay for it. The cabanas on the beach are 250+ dollars for one day. They have completely misunderstood the concept of “all inclusive”. It’s a literal scam. Another issue is how outdated the resort is, it needs massive repair and renovations. The walls are leaking, doors are falling apart and bathrooms are never cleaned consistently. Me and my husband came to Cancun last year and stayed at “live aqua” and it was the best experience ever and therefore, we decided to come back to Cancun and since this time we were traveling with family, we decided to stay at paradisus. Overall, very inconsistent, rude service and overall unpleasant experience for us.

reviews.author: Tom Hong
reviews.text:
I could tell the place used to be nice, but the way it has aged the building is falling apart.  You could see a lot of spots in the complex that were leaking.  Including in our room when it rained there was water leaking into the room and all they did was mop up the water.
We advised several times that the mini fridge was broken and they didn't do anything about it.
The only good thing was the food, which was okay.  We tried all the restaurants (except for the steakhouse) and they were all good along with the service.
Restaurants would not change my opinion in coming back to the facility.  An aged resort that really needs major face lift.

reviews.author: Lukasz Jagiello
reviews.text: Super outdated hotel and not very clean. It’s my 3rd stay in Meliá property and by far it’s the worst one. Super crowded, line to get to breakfast was 1.5h+, dinner at buffet at 9:30 was still with a line for 15min. The staff completely don’t know what to do with the chaos. Food wise everything is not seasoned, dried, without any taste. Really horrible experience but if you’re going to pay extra $270 for cabana suddenly the food is good again so they just don’t care about regular guests.

reviews.author: Ryan Rahim BA e-PRO ABR and PSA
reviews.text:
Where do I start? We had a 2 hour wait time to check in. We were promised an ocean view room and they said no to that because they had a convention and did not have the original room for me. Then they gave me a room on the bottom floor that faced a grass hill that smelled like mold in the room. I told them that I could not stay in that room because the mold smell was too strong they knew about this and agreed. They were able to accommodate finally after the day was over. Our new room was OK and had an ocean view. I was happy for the moment. Till all the problems begin. The toilet handle broke 3 times and the toilet got stopped up 1 time. Our wrist bands did not work 4 different times and we had to go to the lobby to get it fixed multiple times and we were in the farthest tower. They overbooked this hotel and have 1.5 hour or more wait time for restaurants and do not allow you to reserve them. The next option is to go to the buffet, which the food was ok. There were multi leaks throughout the various towers/ building. They do have pros to this hotel... the pool/beach is amazing, the staff is overall very nice. The main pyramid was nice. Overall pictures in general and what you think you are getting are a little off. I would consider a newer hotel or better brand. Will not visit this brand of hotel again. Wish I could tell you differently.
P.S. As I was being asked to listen to an hour presentation of the hotel there were leaks and a garbage can collecting the water right next to the sales person thought that was hilarious.. What a sales pitch. LOL!

reviews.author: Jenna Grounds
reviews.text:
I contemplated writing a review but I wouldn’t want anybody to experience what I did.

Pros - Lily, she is one of the most accommodating and responsive associates I came across here. She is the reason why I didn’t leave on my second day here.
The food is okay, it’s not terrible.
The beach area is beyond kept and beautiful, the waves are rough here though so if you like to swim at the beach then this isn’t for you.
Amenities are good
The smell of the reserve area was everything
The sunset cruise was included free of charge
This hotel is aesthetically gorgeous.

Cons -
We arrived early to check in (11a) and were told to wait 4 hours for our room…… requested a Manager and never talked to one, I practically had to get up and find one… never found one, I then met Lily and expressed my concern.
The quality of food and food options.
There are up charges all throughout the hotel which negatively impacted my experience. We were incorrectly charged for 2 drinks at Cielo, which was about $55. (Picture below)
The staff basically ignored us at the pool area
The pool is very WARM and low in elevation
The drinks are not top shelf, just full of sugar. They have bars with top shelf but will charge you about $20 per shot. They have coconuts at the Beach and charge you $10 for these and only have coconut water????
My room was so HOT (80°F precisely), we called on maintenance 4 times throughout our stay and had to request fans. We couldn’t even leave our window open.
The property could use  updating
The adults steakhouse has minimal options with subpar food, the best food was honestly the pool restaurant and Mexican.
There is no beach attendant??
They advertised cabanas to be included with The Reserve but this solely means pool cabanas and They must be reserved 24 hours in advance, the beach view are $160 and you have to buy a food package… at a resort?? ALSO they have 6 whole chairs that lay flat for tanning, the rest are permanently adjusted at an angle.
The towels in the bathroom are ROUGH
Oh, also transportation is not included as advertised on their website so expect $100+
There was an issue also with my room upgrade, I requested and paid for an ocean view with 2 beds. I was then emailed and quoted a lower price by their in house reservation team and they did not offer a refund or credit for the difference I paid.. instead I was charged for the upgrade a second time upon checking Out and They practically held us and held our transportation until this was resolved. I showed the emails, receipts, and conversation but was treated less than human.

I mean I could go on for days.

Overall, I would not stay here again or recommend it. There are hotels that check boxes of all necessities needed to enjoy your stay. (This is coming from someone who’s traveled to Mexico over 20 times). Expect a bill at check out… even though this is a all inclusive resort.

reviews.author: Luciana
reviews.text:
This hotel does not offer the same quality and service than in the past. The favorite word of the waitresses is “there is no more” . They constantly run out of simple food like avocado or salmon. I cant believe that a 5 star hotel doesn’t have basic foods and they constantly run out of stuff early in the day. No avocado in the morning at 9:00 am and no more salmon for lunch at 13:00. Food tastes average or disgusting. They dont offer good quality licors. If you ask for a cocktail with a good vodka they are spiking it with a low quality alcohol behind your back (i found them doing this). The majority of the waitresses treat you like they are doing you a favor. We are in the adult section paying higher prices and its simply not worth it.
Save yourself your money and dont come here. Price quality NOT WORTH IT.

reviews.author: Jacqueline Burandt
reviews.text:
I am 75 years old and spent my first visit (Christmas Eve 2023) to Paradisus Cancun cold and uncomfortable on a pull out sofa with no sheets, blankets, or cover of any kind. I called three separate times, even spoke with a supervisor,  to ask for covers.  Each time I was told they were coming.  They never came.  I had to get towels from the bathroom to cover up.

The next morning I asked the maid why there were no covers in the room already for the sofa bed and she said it was because they didn't know if someone would be using the sofa bed.  This makes no sense because we booked the room for 3 people.

I complained to everyone in person the next day and was told they would make it up to me by delivering an amenity, a bottle of champagne, to my room. This was hardly sufficient considering I got little sleep.  They didn't deliver champagne--only a bottle of Merlot-- which none of us drinks. I complained to many people over the five days we were there and NEVER received anything different.

There were very several large leaks in the hallways that we had to step over the whole time we were there. There were 3 or 4 bathrooms next to Sal, the very nice restaurant, and not one of them had any toilet paper. I had to tell the restaurant manager.
There were 5 empty plastic cups outside our room for days.  I finally threw them away myself.

The restaurant situation was EXTREMELY frustrating.  They do not accept reservations at the inclusive restaurants which is ridiculous. On  2 nights we bought the all inclusive pass and could not get a seat at any restaurant--we tried them all-- without a 2 hour wait. One of these nights we ate at the buffet out of desperation--never again. The food was inedible--overcooked, tasteless.  When we complained we were told that it was it was the Christmas holidays. Surely hotel management could have planned for this. We ate at SAL (pricey and not included)two nights and while expensive, the food and service were outstanding.

My impression of this hotel was very bad. Everyone paid "lip service" to wanting to exceed our expectations.  No one actually did anything to meet our minimum expectations.  Sheets are really not too much to ask.

I don't ever want to go back.

reviews.author: Ellie Booth
reviews.text:
We recently traveled here with our kids during Spring Break. I have some positive feedback and some  not positive feedbacks. First off we have stayed in other paradisus before, this our first time in this Cancun hotel. It was a beautiful hotel, Beautiful beach and fun pool atmosphere for the kids. Although getting up at 630 daily on vacation to get chairs at beach and pool was quite frustrating. I know this comes with the timing.  We upgraded for Nikte service. Daniel was great to work with and he did every request we asked of him. By day two he really stepped it up.
I can’t imagine what our days would’ve been if we did not have him. Luis at the pool was also awesome in helping us with cabanas daily! They get 5 stars. We unfortunately can only give the food to one star. We honestly struggled with this food as we have been to Mexico over 10 times and this is our first time where we really couldn’t find food that we liked for us in our family, ( minus the pizza bar) we would fill up on this as was only really confident option for us.
my husband actually got food poisoning at the Buffet the first night eating raw  fajitas Unfortunately has been treated for a parasite and been sick for 12 days
The buffet was just so inconsistent, and seems like they brought in the garbage for spring breakers.  The Italian restaurant was rough on service and served raw pizza.  We we’re definitely disappointed with the food so unfortunately will not recommend this location. My son was charged as an adult at 15 and so we spent a lot for a full week and we all lived on pizza.  I have much more to say. But if you a foodie, I wouldn’t choose this location

reviews.author: Ashley A
reviews.text: The service at this hotel made up for everything being a bad hotel experience. We attended this hotel with 3 other groups and each of them had a problem with their rooms. The AC would leak a lot of water, AC would feel hot and cold, one of the rooms had a roach, & the lights would stop working at a certain time. We also paid extra for an ocean view just to realize our door wouldn’t open properly so we couldn’t open the door the whole trip. The looks of the pictures and the price we paid did not meet our expectations. This was the most we have ever spent on a hotel and can say we have seen way better. The food from the buffet (being all inclusive) could have also been WAY better. Paying the amount of money we did, we had expected the food to be very good.

reviews.author: Abolfazl Ghazi
reviews.text:
The restaurants had very long wait time, we waited 2hrs) for dinner especially on the weekends. The telephone line in our room was not working and despite our request and follow up it got repaired 1 hour before our checkout. So we couldn’t use room service during our stay and for any question we had to go downstairs. We were given late checkout for 1hr instead!
The towels were taken the day before departure so I had to go and find someone to get some towels!
We saw two cockroaches right in front of our room.
Most importantly, in the Ginger bar there were some big open windows almost 1ft above floor with no guard, It is really dangerous for the kids if they are left unsupervised for a moment! Picture attached!
Rooms were clean and spacious, bars were good and almost all staff were friendly.

reviews.author: CJ T
reviews.text: I have stayed at this hotel on multiple occasions as it seemed to me to be a benchmark in Canun with respect to; The quality of service, amenities, food, drinks, and comfort—generally speaking, the "plus" service (formerly Royal Service, now The Reserve)—was lacking. I fear this was the last time we were there. The person who greeted us at The Reserve, with a face that suggested they'd been working nonstop for 24 hours (which was likely the case), told us there had been a mistake with the reservations and that they didn't have a room for us in The Reserve. They made us wait almost an hour to see what would happen and then told us they would accommodate us in the standard area with the plus service we had paid for, "a situation that, of course, didn't happen." It's worth mentioning that they moved us on the second night, but what was lost was lost. The quality of the drinks and food has declined drastically. What used to be true room service now resembles a City Express. They didn't even stock the minibars properly. Whereas before you could enjoy, for example, a good wine included in any bar or restaurant, now the entire hotel is served wine of such poor quality that it's best to avoid it. What used to be a truly exquisite breakfast buffet is now, at best, average, and if you want something better, you have to pay extra, like a... The wine for dinner was four times its price, and then, 30 minutes after ordering, they told you they didn't have it, when you were already halfway through your meal. The spa also saw cost-cutting, and it showed. In short, you expect the same level of experience as before, and it's disappointing to see how much money has been cut. Unfortunately, I'll have to look elsewhere.

reviews.author: Sebastian Ripoll
reviews.text:
I'm truly surprised that, given the price, many things aren't included in the "all-inclusive" package. What truly shocks me is that a chain with such a prestigious name offers a cot as a bed for an adult... and the response is that there's nothing to be done about it. One person slept terribly, and on a completely different note, they should have staff on the beach to ensure there are chairs available. It's unbelievable that we can't even go to the beach because of this.

The wine they offer is poor, and the only steakhouse is an extra charge. The services they offer free of charge are unacceptable for a 5-star hotel. It's more like a 3 or 4-star hotel compared to other chains I've stayed at with the same model. At the pool, where people usually gather at lunchtime, there were 20 people waiting during peak hours for just one (yes, only one) person serving. At 11 pm, all the bars close, so they stop serving drinks.

The hotel itself is beautiful. The lobby or main lounge is incredible, with its stunning greenhouse and natural surroundings, and the beach is divine. The water is choppy and rough, not really suitable for children, at least at this time of year.

Unfortunately, I have to return to a Meliá hotel in Punta Cana in a few days, and after this experience, I don't want to go back... Let's see if it's just Mexico or if the whole chain is like this.

reviews.author: koneko Ilustra
reviews.text:
My experience wasn't very good; we were practically ripped off for one night. We had booked the Premium Junior Suite Sunset View, which was supposed to have a jacuzzi and kitchenette, but when we arrived, the room had neither. At reception, we were met with nothing but excuses, claiming the room was in the category we had paid for, but it was obvious it wasn't. They were giving us a lower-category room with fewer amenities. The next day, they moved us to the correct room, but they ruined the experience since we had chosen that room specifically for the jacuzzi, and they didn't even compensate us in any way for their mistake. Honestly, their poor service really dampened the mood of our anniversary trip for the first few days. Several days, they didn't refill the minibar; we had to call room service to get water because they wouldn't refill it.

The other facilities and staff service at the pool and restaurant were very good. I expected the food to be more delicious, but it was just average.

The hotel is very beautiful and its pools are large and spacious, but unfortunately that mistake and poor service in the lobby did affect us. We won't be returning; next time we'll look for other options.

reviews.author: Verónica Aquili
reviews.text: This hotel deserves three stars. The rooms are terrible. We booked a room for four, and it only had two single beds (1.20/1.30 meters wide). The shower didn't work properly, the bedside lamp had exposed wires, and the TV picture was poor. They didn't clean our room, even after we complained. Only after our supplier contacted them did they finally clean it at 9 pm (unacceptable). The food is very good, but you have to queue for everything (unless you're a member or have a membership). Getting a sun lounger is a nightmare (unless you're a member or have a membership). I truly felt disappointed and ripped off during this experience. I'm hoping for a room change today so I can finally get some rest.

reviews.author: JAS M
reviews.text:
My stay at the Paradisus Cancun began on April 26th, accompanied by three friends in two rooms for two nights. Unfortunately, the experience fell short of expectations for a hotel of this category.

From the moment of check-in, the service left much to be desired: there were nearly 20 people waiting to be attended to and only two receptionists available. The process took more than 30 minutes, and the staff's treatment was unfriendly, even disrespectful at times. A terrible first impression.

The hotel's design has its merits, especially in its central area, which is visually appealing. However, the rest of the complex is far from luxurious and shows clear signs of neglect in various areas.

One of the weakest points was the food. The buffet not only offered little variety, but the hot dishes were cold, and what should have been kept cold arrived lukewarm. Furthermore, the absence of seafood such as prawns was disappointing. The service from the restaurant staff was also poor.

As for the pools, although they were in good condition, finding a free lounge chair after 11 a.m. was virtually impossible, which negatively impacted the overall experience.

In short, I would not recommend this hotel nor would I consider returning. There are many areas for improvement, especially in guest service, food quality, and general maintenance of the property.

reviews.author: Aline Rigolo Aline
reviews.text: Não vale o preço. Filas para restaurantes, comidas com pouco sabor, com baixa qualidade, cadeiras de praia reservadas com toalhas tendo que sair do quarto as 7am para reservar se não fica sem e senta no chão. As cabanas tem que pagar valor a parte de 300 dólares para uso, e enquanto você fica no chão elas ficam vazias. Atendimento ruim, poucos funcionários para muitas pessoas. Não indico!

reviews.author: Joel Lessa
reviews.text:
We had to request a room change due to an excessive moldy smell, and the receptionist treated us very unwillingly. The new room flooded during a heavy rain. To make matters worse, they were renovating the room above ours, and the noise started at 7:30 in the morning.
Most of the staff provided terrible service, some with considerable rudeness.
For the hotel's standard, we expected a better experience.

reviews.author: Mariano SP
reviews.text:
Poor value for money.

The worst part is the quality of the food and drinks; calling it poor would be an understatement. The only halfway decent things are the beer and tequila.
Depending on your room's location, you'll have views of the sea or the garbage dump of the hotel next door... And finally, the beach belonging to the hotel barely has any sand and there are always waves, as it's the open-sea side, so the red flag has been up since the hotel was built.

The best things are the pools, the casino, and the beach club, although don't expect more than a bunch of drunk tourists, though it might be good for getting a tequila buzz...

As I said, excessively expensive for what it offers. Around $700 USD for 3 nights at the end of January, which I assume is low season.

I wouldn't stay at this hotel again. There are better options at better prices...

reviews.author: LEVI
reviews.text:
This hotel didn't have many Korean guests, so I'm leaving a review for future reference.

- Pros: 1) This was my first time in Cancun, so I hadn't tried other hotels. Perhaps because it's in the hotel zone, the ocean was incredibly beautiful. The white sand was also fine. 2) It's relatively inexpensive compared to other all-inclusive hotels.

- Cons: 1) The food was the hardest part. The buffet wasn't as good as the buffets at good Korean hotels, but it was decent. However, the menu doesn't change much, so you might get bored quickly. Aside from the Mexican restaurant, I tried the seafood, Italian, and Japanese restaurants, and they were all disappointing. I thought it might be a matter of taste, based on previous Korean blog reviews, but for me, it just wasn't tasty.
2) If you stay in Building 3, which is the main building, music can be loud until late. During our stay, we had trouble falling asleep due to a performance, including percussion instruments, that lasted until 11 p.m. The music isn't just audible; it can also vibrate, which can be a challenge if you're staying with children.
3) The hotel's pool isn't extensive, but it's spacious. However, there's a significant difference in the depth of the children's pool and the other pools. The non-children's pool was about 1.6-1.8 meters deep. There are no other pool facilities suitable for children.
4) The ocean view from the terrace in Building 3, where I stayed, was excellent, but the facilities were lacking for a five-star hotel. The window frames were very worn and wouldn't open or close properly.
5) The staff seemed friendly on the surface, but for a five-star hotel, it was disappointing. There wasn't a dedicated staff member, and the other staff members didn't seem to be proactive in resolving issues.

- And while this isn't necessarily a positive or negative point, the majority of guests at this hotel seemed to be Mexicans. I saw a few Koreans, but not a noticeable number.

reviews.author: annischnulliable
reviews.text:
The numerous positive reviews here largely come from guests who were asked by the staff to leave a good rating. This apparently influences the staff's pay or evaluations, but unfortunately, it doesn't reflect the hotel as a whole!

The price-performance ratio is completely off (anymore). You can see that the hotel once had its heyday, but those days are over.

There aren't enough sun loungers and parasols for everyone; this has apparently been a complaint in reviews for years, and nobody seems to care. We were at the hotel before the peak season, and even then, there weren't enough parasols. It's hard to imagine what it will be like when the hotel is fully booked.

During our stay, an Indian wedding was being held; one pool area was closed for the day, and there were no alternatives other than cramming around the pool like sardines—without any sun protection, of course. Apparently, you couldn't move the parasols from one pool to another. Tough luck, or rent a Bali Bed for the absolutely ridiculous and irrational $250 USD per day. Completely overpriced and, given the circumstances, an absolute outrage!

The staff couldn't care less that there wasn't enough space or sun protection. They suggested we rent a Bali Bed, but otherwise, the only response was always, "Sorry, we have a wedding." Great for the wedding party, but disruptive for ALL the other guests!

The restaurant by the closed pool remained open; so after a "wonderful" day, we had to either shout at each other or remain silent during dinner, as the wedding was in full swing and extremely loud right next to the restaurant.

We saw a total of four rooms, all of which were substandard.

In the first room, we were greeted by a cockroach and an overwhelming smell of paint, as if the last brushstroke had been applied just five minutes earlier. Tired and exhausted from our journey, we asked for an upgrade to the Oceanside room (at an extra cost, of course) and hoped for a better one. After three days of puddles in the room, we heard a drip—it was dripping from the ceiling right next to the bed, presumably from the balcony of the room above. We also discovered that the balcony door was leaking and responsible for the puddles in the room.

We asked to be shown another room, but it also had a leaky door and water in the room. We refused and demanded a refund for the upgrade. They offered us a room on the top floor, supposedly in the highest category. There, too, the door leaked and water was in the room. Tired and annoyed by the whole situation, we agreed to the room without a refund. At least it was a bit quieter up there, and the minibar had slightly better snacks.

Every one of the four rooms had defects, from broken clothes hooks and a shower that couldn't be adjusted properly to a leaky balcony door that sometimes wouldn't open fully (this was fixed after we pointed it out). But for the prices, plus the extra cost for the "upgrade" to an ocean view room, it was simply too poor.

The facade is crumbling everywhere, and it's leaking. Both pools aren't full enough to keep the water clean when draining through the edges.

There are too few sun loungers by the sea, and some of the parasols are buried so deeply in the sand that you can't lie under them. However, Bali Beds are available for $250 USD per day.

The restaurants ranged from very good (Italian) to mediocre. The selection of vegetarian dishes definitely needs improvement!

The coffee bar is open 24/7 and very good, but unfortunately sponsored by Nespresso (Nestlé).

The service from the restaurant and pool staff was mostly good and attentive. There were a few exceptions, but that's to be expected everywhere.

Given these circumstances, we wouldn't book this hotel again.

reviews.author: RicaH
reviews.text:
It used to be a hotel where the food and the staff's friendliness stood out! Now the rooms are archaic, the furniture is old and outdated, and the bathroom mirror is stained from age!

The staff is not friendly at all, except in a few departments.
The food is generally good, but not exceptional; Malva's menus are repetitive!
The beach is full of seaweed; they don't even seem to make an effort to collect what washes up on the sand to make the experience more pleasant.

Everything is overpriced; renting a beach chair costs $250 for a day—outrageous!

All the drinks have artificial flavors!

The reception staff are unfriendly, even upon arrival.

reviews.author: Karla Lopez
reviews.text: The place is lovely and the rooms are quite spacious, although the air conditioning doesn't work very well and the water runs everywhere when you shower, which is why they provide a ton of towels. Despite being an all-inclusive experience, they didn't even refill the minibar water, my room didn't have an iron (although they kindly brought one), and I had to wait about 30 minutes. Furthermore, the food has a huge area for improvement. It's bland and always served cold, plus the service is incredibly slow; the restaurants close very early and they're understaffed. We waited an hour for a table, even though there were about 30 empty tables due to staff shortages, and it took an hour and a half to be served, plus the wine was cold. It's worth noting that only the buffet is open to everyone; without a reservation, you probably won't be able to eat lunch or dinner at the other restaurants. As usual, you arrive at the buffet and, plate in hand, they take all the food from the bar because they were about to close, which was quite rude since the place wasn't closed yet, and the waitress left me with the sauce spoon in my hand and took it away. Anyway, for the price, there are many other better options in the area.

reviews.author: Javier Sanchez
reviews.text: Paradisus advertises itself as a 5-star all-inclusive hotel, which is completely false. In reality, it has many things to improve before it can truly be called that. Today is March 4, 2025, and we just returned from a 3-night stay. From the very first day, I wanted to leave. I've stayed at several resorts in Mexico, and this one has been the most boring, exploitative, and with terrible service from the staff. I found it very strange that the employees were so rude and provided such poor service, but it's the hotel's fault because they are understaffed, especially in the beach area. In every other resort I've been to, except this one, there's a beach bar and snack area where you can go and order whatever you want or serve yourself, but not here. Since we had to order from a single waiter who was serving everyone on the beach, and you order something and it takes forever to get it... so we decided to go up and order and get our own drinks and snacks, but they wouldn't give us anything because, according to our waiter, he had to bring it to us. So our time at the beach was terrible. Another thing I didn't like is that they don't have any entertainment except the shows, which, by the way, they give you a QR code to check schedules and locations, and then you go and find out that the entire program and locations are different; and the three days we were there, they scheduled the international restaurants at the times the shows started, and we either went to the show or the restaurants, which was awful! The shows are the only free entertainment they have! Since they don't have anything else! That's why we were super bored, and there was an area called Escape, I think it was, and we went there so my daughter would be entertained. It turns out it cost money... super expensive, $800 per person! I mean, they charge for everything: a sunbed, room service, games, and I was even afraid to ask the waiters anything because they always want tips for everything. If you don't have cash in hand, nobody moves. Don't operate like an all-inclusive resort! Don't scam tourists!
