I saw all the foreigners there struggling just like us, and besides, they didn't have enough sunbeds; they were all strewn on the sand because there wasn't enough space. And the spaces they did have cost $250 each—it's a total rip-off! There was no entertainment on the beach, no music; that was only in the areas where you pay $250 for your sunbed. We found a cockroach in our room, the food in the restaurants was terrible in both taste and variety, and only one restaurant was open; you had to make a reservation for all the others. Suddenly, in any area of ​​the hotel you walked around—tables, chairs, etc.—they told you it was reserved because someone had already paid. Honestly, I've been to much cheaper resorts with top-notch service; this hotel was nothing like it. The only thing we liked was the beach water, and that was only because it wasn't theirs. I feel bad for all the other foreigners I saw because they were treated the same way; they must have been very disappointed.

reviews.author: Jorge L. Cisneros Encalada
reviews.text: It's not all-inclusive; once inside, you pay extra for some food, there are access restrictions that force you to pay extra, the restaurants are clean but the food costs extra, half the staff are unhelpful, you have to make reservations for everything, wait in line, and hope you can find a spot. If you want to sunbathe on a lounge chair, you have to get up at 6 am and go reserve one because by 7:30 am there are none left, and that means paying 5,000 Mexican pesos for a few beds (of which there are many, taking up space from the "all-inclusive" lounge chairs). The room always has water leaking from a hole, the pools are dirty, in fact, one smells like sewage. In short, a bad average; I won't be back. There are some kind and attentive people, but they are few and far between.

reviews.author: Uriel García
reviews.text:
I'd like to start with the positive points:
- The hotel is very beautiful, with great views of the beach. The lobby and the main pyramid are among the best in Cancun.

- The Lemon Fish restaurant has a beautiful design and delicious food.

The negative points:
- In general, the service from the waiters is mediocre to poor. They take a long time to serve you in all the restaurants and on the beach.

- The room service is very bad. Once I ordered at night and they made a mistake. I waited almost two hours only to receive nothing.

- The woman at the Calzone pizzeria had a terrible attitude. While I was placing my order, I overheard other guests making negative comments about her.

- If you want to dine out at any of the restaurants, you have to be prepared to wait, as they all have a wait of more than an hour and a half, and the hostesses are also very unfriendly.

- The air conditioning in my room wasn't working properly. We filed a report with reception, but no one ever came to check it.

reviews.author: Tamara fernandez jimenez (Curiosidadesporuntubo)
reviews.text:
I'll start by highlighting the hotel's strengths: location and staff.

However, the hotel itself leaves much to be desired, to the point where I wonder if it truly deserves its 5-star rating.

I stayed in The Reserve option, and that's what I'll focus on.

Something they advertise as so exclusive falls far short of expectations:

- At the pool, staff constantly try to sell things: drone photos, excursions, spa services (they repeat this every day, making it seem like they're getting a commission for selling you something). In a place like The Reserve, where you pay more, this shouldn't be allowed.

- The rooms are old. The air conditioners are very loud. I ran out of shower gel and was without it for two days; they didn't refill it until I complained. My room wasn't cleaned for two days, and I notified them on those same days that they could come and clean it at 4:00 PM, but no one showed up. A cockroach appeared in the room.

- Does an exclusive service like The Reserve really deserve this level of service at this price?

On the other hand, regarding the common areas:

- During our stay, a piece of the hallway ceiling literally fell off (photo attached).

- There are numerous leaks throughout the ceilings (you can see this because there are wet marks all over the floor).

- In addition to my room, I saw two more cockroaches in the hallways (photo attached).

- Another day, we rode in the elevator next to a sponge that I don't know where it came from (photo attached).

- Also, during our stay, the gym was closed and moved to another location where only half the machines remain.

In short, the hotel has a good location and the staff is friendly. The hotel itself is not a 5-star hotel, as it is old and leaves much to be desired for the price (there are better options in the area), and The Reserve category is not worth it at all, as you won't receive the service you expect.

reviews.author: Alex
reviews.text: The hotel is fine, but the service is poor. They don't have 24-hour service, they run out of food, and they don't offer any solutions. The manager is useless, not even noticing that they're out of food. The restaurants close before the closing time they tell you when you pay. In summary, a very nice building, very poor service. For example, in the sandwich area, they have sandwiches on display that are unusable because they're so old, they tell you so themselves.

reviews.author: Erika G
reviews.text:
The hotel is very nice and has a beautiful beach, although upon arrival I saw cockroaches in one of the bathrooms near the lobby, and the restrooms were quite dirty. The ocean-view room was spacious and very clean. This is my second time visiting, and I continue to complain about the TERRIBLE service. If you're a foreigner, I have no doubt they'll treat you like a local, as if you're asking for handouts and your money is worthless.

I think it's excellent that they have a smoking area. The food at Malva was very bad in my opinion, except for Flora, where the service was quick and the food was delicious. Blue Agave was extremely slow, and it really annoyed me to go for four tacos and be kept waiting for over half an hour.

reviews.author: Ilse VK
reviews.text:
Update:
My husband, my daughter, and I contracted the same infection in the hospital. My daughter has been hospitalized. We ate most of our meals at the Maval International Buffet. During our stay, we witnessed another child vomiting at that restaurant. Now I wonder if he, and how many other people, got sick from the food there. On the last day of our stay, while dining at Maval, we saw cockroaches crawling on the restaurant floor. Completely antigenic.

Paradisus Cancun did not meet our expectations. The hotel is very neglected and desperately needs renovations. The hotel is not very clean. The rooms are very outdated, the bathrooms are too small, and there is no bathtub available. We stayed at this hotel for 5 days, and for two days the shower only had cold water. We also found a cockroach in our bathroom, another in the main pool, and others in the international buffet (on the floors). After reading other reviews, I realize we are not the only ones who found cockroaches at the hotel.

The view from our Ocean View room was depressing. The balcony was very run down, and we could only see the roof of a building.

The service was generally good. There was a variety of food to choose from most of the time, but the lines at the restaurants were very long. My husband started vomiting and had diarrhea on the fourth day. Apparently, he got food poisoning at the hotel. I haven't had any problems with the food.

When we booked our stay, we purchased an all-inclusive package. We were told the New Year's Eve party was also included, but when we arrived at the hotel, we had to pay $5,000 for two adults to attend the party since the all-inclusive seats had already been reserved. They never explained to us that this could happen.

The service at the New Year's Eve party was very poor. We had to remind our server about our plates several times (the rest of the table had already been served except for us). They also forgot my baby's food and kept us waiting until the end. The entertainment at the party was good.

reviews.author: Daniel Husni
reviews.text:
The hotel looks imposing from the outside. I can't deny it's beautiful, the food is excellent, and everyone goes out of their way to provide great service, but... things can go wrong, and it just so happened to me. I had been assigned a room in tower 3, which is the best of the five. When I went to get the key, they took 20 minutes and told me that since my room was already assigned, they were giving me a better one in tower 4. When I arrived at tower 4, I opened the door with my wristband, and to my surprise, I found a man in his underwear asking me what I was doing in his room! I went back to the lobby, waited another 15 minutes, and they gave me another room in tower 1, which is the furthest away... Tired after a 12-hour trip, I accepted it. I walked 300 meters with my suitcase, feeling hot, and arrived at the room... and no one answered the door. Back to the lobby... They reprogrammed my wristband, and I had to walk another 300 meters with my suitcase to finally get into my room after an hour.

The room is old but spacious and comfortable. It's a shame they gave me one with a lagoon view when I should have had an ocean view, both the original one they didn't give me and the one the man in his underwear was in.
The hotel doesn't offer any activities, and everything closes at 11 pm.
Another issue is that I wanted to ask for a towel on the beach, and there weren't any left, so I had to wait 20 minutes.
I ordered nachos on the beach, and they took another 20 minutes... The TV isn't a smart TV, and there's no streaming service. The balcony has a Jacuzzi, but the problem is that when I used it, the whole balcony flooded because it had leaks.
All of this is unacceptable for a hotel that costs US$500 a night.

I definitely did not have a good experience

reviews.author: Roberto Gonzalez
reviews.text:
Very bad experience at the hotel; the all-inclusive package wasn't fully delivered. There were too many guests, which overwhelmed the services.
There were very few lounge chairs at the pools and beach, forcing people to rent VIP lounge chairs ($250 per day). Waiting to get into a restaurant could take up to three hours (Lemon Fish, Cielo, Agua Marina), and many guests were understandably frustrated and went elsewhere. The food at some restaurants, like Blue Agave or Lunch Box, lacked the quality expected of a luxury hotel (we even spoke with the manager). The minibar wasn't restocked for two days. However, the staff (waiters, bartenders, and cleaning staff) gave more than 100%, going above and beyond to provide the best service, yet they were poorly compensated, which showed in their exhaustion. On the other hand, it wasn't all bad; we arrived well before 3:00 PM and our room was ready, very comfortable, and clean. I am leaving this place very sad and disappointed. Even during our stay, we went to guest services and they literally just gave us the runaround.

reviews.author: ana livia dacar roldan
reviews.text:
The hotel is very poor in quality and has limited food options. We arrived on December 11th and for the first 5 days there were no lunch or dinner options, only food that you can eat at any cafeteria for 10 reais in Brazil. There are no reasonable drink options, all soft drinks are served flat.
Only after the fifth day at the hotel was a large restaurant reopened with more food options, but with the same terrible quality of service and lines longer than the SUS (Brazilian public health system) - because when they opened this one, they closed the others. It takes more than 1 hour and 30 minutes for a simple meat order to arrive.
It is clear that they do everything to prevent you from consuming food and drinks freely...to give you an idea, the Nutella is kept on a frozen table to make it harder than a rock, precisely so that you can't get anything more than a few pieces. Ice cream can only be found in the middle of the hotel, far from the leisure areas. The kids' and baby zone areas are also extremely far away, and the activities are almost nonexistent.
There are times throughout the day when there is nothing to eat, and the café is only open until 5 pm.
I recommend looking for another hotel. I will never return... we still have 2 days left and we can't stand it anymore.

reviews.author: Lourdes C
reviews.text:
I had very high expectations for this hotel, but it disappointed me.
From check-in, which took hours.
I saw a comment above that perfectly described my experience.
The rooms need updating; the electrical outlets are old, the vanity doesn't even have a mirror, the shower curtain is inadequate so water leaks out, the air conditioner is practically useless, and the mini-fridge is quite basic.
And the service? Not to mention the service. We asked for different sheets twice, and they only left the sheets on. They only came to change them on the third call. We're supposed to be on vacation, not cleaning the room or making the beds.
Housekeeping was late, and sometimes they didn't come at all. There were no spots left in the pool area before 8:00 AM. There aren't enough lounge chairs, and they do it on purpose so they can charge $250 USD per day for a Balinese bed; they practically gave me a room for that! Outrageous! Where have you ever seen anything like this?

The only thing I liked was the buffet.
I wouldn't go back.

reviews.author: Gabriela
reviews.text: The hotel is old and needs maintenance in many aspects. In my case, the curtains in my room were dirty, nothing serious, but something I really didn't like was the immediately noticeable difference in treatment between domestic and foreign tourists, which I find rude since all guests pay the same. In addition, the restaurant hours are strict, and half an hour before closing time they're already pressuring you to leave, clearing away your belongings and even closing off areas, preventing you from reaching your table. Honestly, I will never stay there again.

reviews.author: Tatiana Bolivar
reviews.text: For the price, the hotel wasn't great. The hotel has no air conditioning; it was incredibly hot. Only the rooms had a little air conditioning, and even then, it felt like it was faulty. The bathroom is very old; it flooded every time I showered. Customer service was good, though. Plus, everything closes at 11 pm. We couldn't enjoy our stay to the fullest.

reviews.author: Antonio Lopes
reviews.text: This hotel is 35 years old and urgently needs renovation. The food service (restaurants) is very poor and insufficient. The food items are always the same, with few daily changes. There are daily queues to get to breakfast, lunch, and dinner, or to avoid these queues you have to eat very early. Some of the restaurants, inexplicably, are closed, or close for dinner, throwing guests into queues or waiting lists to get a meal, which is very bad. Otherwise, the staff are friendly, and they are the best aspect of the hotel, along with the location.

reviews.author: Pedro Ramírez
reviews.text:
Overall, a bad experience. The hotel's room capacity far exceeds the space in its restaurants. I had to wait in lines for over 20 minutes to get into the breakfast area, and they ran out of towels at the pool. On one occasion, I had to walk back to my room soaking wet. This happened on a random weekend; it wasn't even peak season.

The hotel is nice, but it shows its age. On the day of my check-out, they had problems with the water supply in my room. I had to speak to more than three people, and it took them two hours to resolve the issue. Because of this, I didn't have time to wait in line at their restaurant and ended up going to McDonald's for breakfast (which really annoyed me since I had paid for an all-inclusive package to be carefree). All of this happened during a three-day stay, and I have no desire to return. I'm giving it two stars because the staff was very friendly; the main problem, I think, is the hotel's infrastructure.

reviews.author: Lb Gonzalez
reviews.text: The hotel in general, I imagine judging by the plants in the hallways, has a suffocating musty smell. Aside from that, everything was fine until we checked out. We approached our boss, who was staying a couple more days (it was a business trip), to get his instructions. We hadn't even been there five minutes when hotel staff approached us and arrogantly told us we had no business being there and couldn't order anything (of course we weren't ordering anything; we already had our bags ready to leave). They asked us to leave. So we left the premises and waited outside until it was time to go to the airport. As long as you pay, everything is friendly; as soon as you check out, you're in the way.

reviews.author: Mariana Henriquez
reviews.text:
I went to Paradisus with high expectations, as I have experience with hotels of this type.

I had several issues at the hotel:
- I had a flight in the early morning, so I wanted to be able to stay a few extra hours at the hotel to avoid being at the airport for 12 hours. We mentioned this at reception and to our butler, who told us we should book for another night, which I did. On the last day, when I went to check out, the person at reception told me I could stay until 5 pm, and that they even had showers available. Nobody informed me of this beforehand, not even the butler; he was only interested in selling us a club membership.

- One day the power went out practically all day; there was no water, air conditioning, or frozen drinks. How is it possible that a 5-star hotel doesn't have a floor dedicated to such situations?

- Smoking area: I don't smoke, but my partner does. So I agree that smoking shouldn't be allowed in areas like the pool or the restaurant. However, I find it absurd that smoking isn't allowed on the balconies or the beach. Furthermore, if they're going to create a smoking area, the least they can do is make it decent, provide shade, and have lighting at night.

- Noise: While smoking is prohibited for the well-being of others, the same doesn't apply to noise. When I was there, a group of kids arrived with a huge speaker and blasted their music by the pool, making the place unbearable. None of the employees were able to tell them off.

- Turtles: This coast of Cancun is one of the nesting sites for loggerhead turtles, an endangered species. They lay their eggs, and when they hatch, they become disoriented by the hotel lights and, instead of going to the beach, end up trapped on the hotel stairs. Several nights we went down to the beach and found hundreds of turtles in this situation, which we helped return to the sea. The hotels in the area should have staff or volunteers available to help with this at night, as many turtles get trapped or flipped over.

reviews.author: Edvin TT
reviews.text: The staff needs more training because they're not friendly at all and don't care about the guests. The restaurants... mmm, the menu they offer is very limited, and the dishes are served in miniature. And room 211? It needs improvements. The toilet was leaking, the jacuzzi wasn't working, the refrigerator was very noisy, the shower door hit the floor when you opened it, and we told them all about it. They said they would check it, but they never did. Very bad service.

reviews.author: Andres Zamora
reviews.text:
My two stars are for:
1) This is not a smoking hotel. There are some pretty absurd restrictions. The entire hotel only has two designated smoking areas, and neither offers any shade. It's 36 degrees Celsius under a blazing sun. Trying to smoke a cigarette is more torture than pleasure.

2) The hotel doesn't have staff to care for baby turtles. I came across hundreds of baby turtles while walking at night. These turtles get lost in the hotel grounds because the light confuses them, and many end up dying on the hotel steps. I spent nights trying to rescue many lost turtles. While the hotel has a very small section where they look after several nests, they aren't equipped to handle the problem along the entire hotel's shoreline. There are many other nesting sites besides the one where they come to lay their eggs. Let's remember that these are critically endangered species. I don't understand how a 5-star hotel doesn't prioritize this above all else. It's their responsibility, at the very least, to take care of their section of the beach. It's disrespectful to nature not to commit to caring for them and saving 100% of the turtles that are born there.

3) Almost all the areas have places they call "the reserve," and these places have additional charges. It's absurd that you have to pay anything at an all-inclusive resort. The name itself says it all. Everything should be included. Almost all the hotels in the area have something similar. But at this hotel, it's sometimes quite absurd.

4) The electricity went out for an entire day. I don't understand how they aren't prepared for these situations. They should have solar panels that help protect the ecosystem and allow them to cope with these situations. I didn't see anything eco-friendly, other than the fact that they don't allow smoking. It's absurd that the hotel doesn't consider the most important thing in terms of helping the environment.

reviews.author: Jaime Guerra
reviews.text:
To be honest, the rooms are comfortable and the facilities are nice; the pool is quite large and beautiful. Even the gym is decent for a hotel gym. Overall, the facilities are comfortable; however, the food service is TERRIBLE. Two restaurants were closed. The first day we ate at a taco stand, and the tacos were so meager and scarce that the tacos at almost any other taqueria are better. That same day we had dinner at the Market Grill, which they claim is an Argentinian and Brazilian grill, but all they had to eat was rice, beans, and just one meat dish. We complained to the manager about how poor and neglected the food bar was, and the next day they offered us a barbecue as an apology, but other than that, everything else remained the same. For breakfast, they only served eggs, and when they were feeling generous, they had carnitas, but they didn't serve the sides. So, if you want to eat just eggs or pancakes every day, you'll be fine. There are no vegetable options, only "roasted vegetables," which are just squash; there's no other variety. You have to make a reservation for dinner, but there was never any room to try a different restaurant, and we ended up eating at Enzo every day. The Asian food was poor and bland, with nothing interesting about it. The best dessert at this restaurant was the rice pudding, because even the ice cream was ordinary, with an artificial flavor and a buttery taste, just like the gelato they serve at the gelato shop, which isn't Italian but the ugliest Mexican ice cream. The poolside snack bar is neglected and poorly run; the lettuce looks abandoned, and the tomatoes float in the juice that accumulates because the person in charge can't remove it to keep the vegetables fresh and appetizing. There weren't any vegetables either. At the sushi restaurant, they offer a side of vegetables, but if you ask for them, they don't put them on your plate. It's 6 pm and there are no towels at the pool. They also close the pool ridiculously early, at 7 pm, even though it's still daylight.
Unfortunately, during my stay I saw several other people complaining about the poor service, just like I did at the barbecues. I saw plates left on the tables, full of food because people preferred not to eat them. Also, on the first day, while waiting (45 minutes) to check in, a foreign family was very upset and complaining. I overheard casual conversations in the hallways of people commenting on the bad service (I quote, "worst service in town"). There are very few umbrellas at the pool. I don't know if this is intentional, to try to get people to pay for a VIP lounge, which does look comfortable. Finally, they have very aggressive strategies to get guests to attend the famous timeshare sales breakfast, which I didn't have this time on my stay, but on a previous occasion, my wife did accept it. It turned out they pressured her for an hour and a half (when they had said forty minutes) to buy a timeshare, and they also wanted to know everything about us, from where we work to how much we earn. They chase you down the hallways to invite you to breakfast, but they don't do their part to correct all the things I found lacking.

Lastly, and to top it all off, their cocktail service is poor. The drinks are very artificial, and the ingredients they use are just coloring and sugar; they don't have the flavor a good cocktail should have. Honestly, the accommodations are expensive, and although the hotel isn't terrible, the food and drinks don't justify the price.

reviews.author: Eduardo Alcaide
reviews.text:
The good: Mexicans are generally very friendly, and the hotel has an excellent beach.

The bad: very old rooms, very worn beds and cushions. On rainy days, water leaked through the window, and although we asked for a room change, they only put towels on the floor for us to dry off. The pool in front of the Lunch Box is very dirty, to the point that one Sunday a child's diaper tore in the water and wasn't cleaned. We saw the remains of the diaper floating until Tuesday, the day we left. The food in general, with the exception of the hamburgers, wasn't very good. You should be aware that COVID protocols are practically nonexistent at this hotel. There were several things, but this was what shocked us the most.

The insurance they offer is nothing more than a discount to continue staying at the hotel if you contract COVID.

The insurance they offer is nothing more than a discount to continue staying at the hotel if you get COVID. The antigen test they include is not accepted by most countries, so you will have to get a PCR test, which costs $90 per person (offered by the hotel upon arrival).

reviews.author: Chimera Ditto
reviews.text:
I understand that there are very busy dates, but from the first day, not only was it incredibly slow to be served at reception, and even the reception manager didn't know how to make keys, but they assigned us to two wrong rooms. One had the wrong beds, and the other was occupied.
We spent well over two hours just waiting. By the time we finally got close to the dining area, they refused to seat us in a very insensitive manner because it was eight minutes past the end of service, without offering an alternative and sending us back to reception if we "had any problems." That day was my birthday. I'd had a headache for three hours already, and with all the reception's mistakes, this really impacted my opinion of Paradisus.
We complained, and they "resolved" things a little by giving us a table we liked for dinner, but the bad service had already happened.

The food is "okay." The only thing I particularly liked was breakfast at La Palapa.

Dinner at the Asian restaurant wasn't great either; the sashimi wasn't fresh. It tasted like water. The ramen wasn't great either; I only really enjoyed the ice cream and the buffet.

reviews.author: Yalilys Mena
reviews.text: We stayed from July 12th to July 19th. The food at this hotel was not to our liking. The buffet table offered little variety, and mashed potatoes and rice were extremely difficult to find. Occasionally, they made yellow rice with vegetables, but it was made with precooked rice that tasted bad. The few times I managed to get it, it was fried rice, and I would ask the waiter for some uncooked rice so my son could eat it. We also didn't like the specialty restaurants that require reservations, and the hamburgers and hot dogs they offer around the pool were equally disappointing. In short, we returned to Miami starving. If you want a spectacular massage at the spa, I recommend the individual massage with a woman named Ana; it will be worth every penny. That's why I encouraged my husband to go for the couples massage, which I DO NOT RECOMMEND. My husband was satisfied, of course, he had no point of comparison, but I did, and I can assure you that the difference was enormous. The professionalism and expertise were evident. Two years ago we went to Punta Cana and stayed at the Barcelo Bavaro, and we didn't want to leave. However, at the Paradisus Cancun, we were desperate to return home. I'm giving it two stars because the ambiance is quite beautiful, and the staff tries hard to meet your needs; otherwise, I'm giving it one star.

reviews.author: GABRIELJOTA Henao
reviews.text:
Excellent buildings and facilities.
The staff is very friendly and attentive; a round of applause for these Mexican people.
The quality of the food in all the restaurants is regrettable. The Market is advertised as a Brazilian Rodizio, but it's nothing like it... the meat is tough, and the salad bar has a very limited selection of vegetables, etc.
The wines are the lowest quality possible. Several guests we met at the pools told us the same thing about the poor quality of the food.

In short, for the price you pay, you don't get good food.

reviews.author: Marcelo Kira
reviews.text: The hotel is okay, but it has an 80s feel. The food is rather bland, you can't use the pools on the left unless you're a Royal member, and there are two restaurants. The beach bungalows are also for Royal members or anyone willing to pay a measly $80 to $150. The central lobby doesn't have air conditioning, and if you go to the Japanese restaurant in that lobby, be prepared to sweat. In short, I don't know if all the resorts in the region are like this, but this one isn't worth R$10,000 a week.

reviews.author: Umut Polat
reviews.text:
I would simply expect more from a 5-star hotel. Compared to hotels in Turkey in this price range, this hotel is inadequate. There are practically no special activities for children, neither in the restaurants nor in the recreation area. The food is rather monotonous. Although 5-6 restaurants are advertised, we weren't truly satisfied with any of the three we visited. You have to fight for salt, as there's only one set of salt and pepper for 50 tables. Some drinks are served with chlorinated water. There's a shortage of sun loungers by the pool, and as mentioned, no proper play area for children.

We booked two tours and, after the first one, realized it was too physically demanding for my pregnant wife. Therefore, we wanted to cancel the second tour. The hotel's on-site tour operator showed absolutely no understanding or flexibility. When we asked the hotel for help, we were simply told that we had to take care of it ourselves. A huge thank you again to the head concierge, Paulina, who couldn't care less. Unfortunately, the beach was unusable due to the seaweed, but that's not the hotel's fault. Generally speaking, the hotel isn't geared towards German tourists, as there don't seem to be many German-speaking providers.

reviews.author: Maria Julia Martinez
reviews.text: The hotel is a bit old and not quite up to par with the one in Playa del Carmen. The main pool area is very crowded, and it's difficult to find shade. The children's play area is very good. The family concierge staff are very friendly. The best rooms are quite small. The restaurants aren't great and close very early. We knew the Paradisus in Playa del Carmen a few years ago, and this one in Cancun was quite disappointing. We didn't like it.

reviews.author: Armando Flores Barrera
reviews.text:
The staff service is terrible!!!
The facilities and furnishings are very nice; it's truly a beautiful hotel. However, all of that is overshadowed and ruined by the awful service from the employees. The waiters are incredibly unhelpful, have no interest in customer service, seem annoyed all the time, and are unempathetic and inattentive. I would return because of the facilities, but because of the service, never!!! I absolutely do not recommend it.

reviews.author: Jannett Jiménez Almaraz
reviews.text: This hotel is huge, but it has NO air conditioning in the common areas and it's incredibly hot. Some restaurants have air conditioning, others don't. The air conditioning in the rooms barely cools, the food quality is "bad"—not even the specialty dishes are any good. The international breakfast buffet is always the same, the ice cream machines are broken, and you practically had to get water. The cafeteria was closed for a whole day. Some of the staff were helpful, others weren't; it seemed like they were doing you a favor. The elevators had unpleasant smells, and the hallways smelled like stagnant water. Some rooms needed maintenance. They charge for everything; you have to get up early to reserve a palapa, and the lounge chairs/large beds cost per day. The shows weren't good. There are exclusive areas of the hotel that you can't enter unless you're a Royal Service guest. There's also an extra charge for the restaurant, and palapas are reserved for a different guest category. I don't recommend it for families or couples, to be honest. This hotel left much to be desired and was very, very expensive! We had stomach problems for two days because of the food, and we saw many other people complaining. In short, NOT recommended. Our stay was from July 15th to 20th. A disappointing vacation; we didn't enjoy it as we should have.

reviews.author: Angel Manuel Cabrera Estévez
reviews.text: This hotel is completely overrated. It has an undeserved reputation, which we found to be entirely false. The excessively hot atmosphere in the facilities, lounges, and hallways (without air conditioning) is disorienting and disturbs the peace of any guest, making one feel completely uncomfortable. The rooms and bathrooms (at least those located in Pyramid #3, where we stayed) are too old, outdated, and in dire need of renovation. The only redeeming feature is the excellent service and facilities provided by the vast majority of the staff, especially those in the bars, restaurants, concierge, and housekeeping departments.

reviews.author: Lucas Ozan
reviews.text: The staff service is very poor. The rooms are adequate. Housekeeping comes at any time, regardless of complaints and agreed-upon schedules. The hotel is well-maintained and has good restaurants. It's a shame that I can't recommend it because of the terrible service.

reviews.author: Claudia Alejandra Fuentes Gimenez (LATAM)
reviews.text: I found a cockroach in my room. The family concierge service is not what it promises. The person assigned to my family was only seen twice; the rest of the time they just forwarded the messages she sent to all the families. She gave us incomplete and confusing information about the Balinese boats. We only received the Balinese boat we requested on the last day (with all the restrictions they had). It's unacceptable that at the hotel buffet you have to queue to get in and even to find food, since part of it was closed. Besides, there was very little variety of food. This is not what you'd expect from a 5-star hotel. The only positive thing about the buffet was Martin's excellent service. I think if they're remodeling, they should inform the customer so they can make an informed decision. I assure you that if I had known, I wouldn't have gone back, since the service I received was not what I paid for.

reviews.author: Lorena Nolasco
reviews.text:
The longest check-in I've ever had. They don't even offer you water (well, when the guy trying to sell you a membership comes along, he'll give you a bottle of water, but forget about a welcome cocktail). There's no bar near the lobby, and no staff to bring you anything. If you want a drink, you have to walk all the way to the pool, which is really far away, to get it, and then come back, obviously, with your drink warm and half-finished. 🤦‍♀️ The rooms were fine, though; the beds and linens were very good quality and very comfortable.

The unforgivable thing is that the "classic" accommodations have three systems: the all-inclusive option, which gives you the same as every other hotel; accommodation with concierge service; and Royal Service. This is awful because it's obvious they only treat those who pay more with special treatment. And of course, they don't let you use the areas reserved for Royal Service guests, which makes you feel uncomfortable and discriminated against. Worse still, they never offer upgrades upon arrival; you don't even realize it until the waiter is already telling you, "Excuse me, you can't be in this area," right in front of you. 😪 They charge you for the minibar at the end, even though there's no sign indicating an extra cost and even though they said it was free over the phone.
They don't have enough lounge chairs, and it's clear they do this intentionally to make you pay extra for a beach bed. On another note, I thought that bad Cancun habit of treating foreigners better than Mexicans had been eradicated, but I was wrong; it's still going strong here.

Overall, I can't recommend them, except for the room, the smell in the reception area, and the bedding. Everything else has its issues, some more annoying than others.
Oh, and if you're traveling with small children, definitely don't go near this hotel. The children's pool is tucked away in the corner and far from everything. There's no water park or anything like that. The kids' zone is nice, and the staff are friendly, but it's all in the basement.

reviews.author: Alberto de la Fuente
reviews.text: I've been waiting for my invoice for two weeks and nothing. I call and they leave me hanging on the phone. I've even sent my tax information for the umpteenth time and nothing. The on-duty supervisor, Guadalupe Rodriguez, promised it to me and nothing. The room division director, Abraham Franco, sent me an empty email and still haven't answered, just like in accounting with Eliana Suastegui. My room, 4202, got flooded when it rained. I tried to book at the restaurants and they were full, and during my stay only two were open per night. Most nights I had to dine at the buffet. It's not the same as when it was Gran Meliá 8-10 years ago. I'd much rather go to Le Blanc or Gran Velas. It's a huge disappointment. I'll be waiting forever for my invoice. Oh, and they force you to book timeshares from the moment you check in, and the reservation on the website doesn't work, so I had to make it over the phone.

reviews.author: Pedro Mora
reviews.text: The place is wonderful, but the service is very poor. I've been fortunate enough to visit different Paradisus resorts (Playa del Carmen and Punta Cana), both as a Meliá Club member and as a guest, but this one has several areas for improvement. It's only a Meliá resort, not a Paradisus. I'm currently on the Royal Service package, but it's not worth paying extra. There's only one bar where you can order premium drinks, which aren't really that premium. Restaurant reservations have to wait because the tables aren't ready. They ask all day if you need anything, and when you ask for it, it arrives late or isn't there. On the beach, you ask for water, and it doesn't arrive until noon. They're also limited in essential items, like a thermometer. They give you one and wait for you to use it before taking it back. When you ask for it again, it's still not there. I can imagine a family with a sick child who needs their temperature monitored. Adults can wait until the night and hope someone goes out to buy one, but a child can't wait. The best thing is the beach and how beautiful Cancun is; this has been the case in the 3 days we have been staying. Let's hope that the 6 days that remain will be somewhat better, because otherwise it would only be 1 star.

reviews.author: Berenice Rodriguez
reviews.text: To be honest, this time the service wasn't what I expected. I've had the opportunity to stay at the same place on several occasions, and the food, service, and facilities have always been excellent. This time, the food wasn't even close to what I expected, breakfast was a mess, and there was little organization or cleanliness. They're repairing the air conditioning in one of the main restaurants, and that's caused chaos. Maybe we'll return later to see if it was just during that one stay.

reviews.author: César Davit SOTO
reviews.text:
This hotel was a huge problem. They wouldn't let me check in because I didn't have the card I used to pay for my stay online. Even though I showed them my bank statement confirming I made the transfer, they assumed I was using a stolen card—awful. They refused to give me my room, and I had to pay again since the rate was non-refundable. When they refunded me the second payment, they reduced it by $60. (Now that I'm back home, there's no one to complain to.)
And to top it all off, three of the restaurants—two of which I returned for—were closed (they were remodeling, and obviously, they're not saying anything). August 2019. I will never return to this hotel, even if it's a registered one.

reviews.author: Marcelo Batista
reviews.text:
It only has fame, the breakfast buffet is simple every day, as is the lunch, the kind where you go around in circles, dinner is better, but nothing luxurious as advertised, many Chinese people must like it.
I speak based on this, it was the 8 Resort and I expected it to be the best and unfortunately it was one of the worst.

reviews.author: Abby Cruz
reviews.text:
How true is it that the hotel is closing?
A waiter said they're laying off staff. So we don't want to risk making our reservations if it's not certain.

reviews.author: Reme SanG
reviews.text: It was awful how the waiters and bartenders treated the Mexicans, Colombians, Peruvians, Argentinians, Costa Ricans, Guatemalans, and others who had paid for everything. To be clear... not all of them, but most. Rude. But those who got tips were treated like royalty. Very sad.

reviews.author: Max Sasa
reviews.text:
The "all-inclusive" package is misleading; it doesn't include some restaurants, beach beds (only lounge chairs), and other things. The service is rather slow. The drinks aren't the best. Overall, I think there are better options for the same price. Compare prices and other hotels before booking here.

——————————-
Thanks for your reply, Jair. Since I couldn't respond any other way, I'm editing my previous post. Regarding what you mentioned about additional services, I agree that any extra service like the ones you mentioned should have an extra cost. But when all you need is a shaded lounge chair because you have a baby with you, and you see that absolutely all the lounge chairs and palapas are occupied (lack of equipment and the hotel is overbooked), what do you do? Do you decide not to go to the beach and the pool even though that was the purpose of your trip? Or do you force yourself to pay $180 USD ($3,600) for a "bed" so that you and your family can be comfortable? I went at the end of February (low season), and I can't imagine how crowded it must be during peak season. If I found it impossible to find a lounge chair then, imagine what it's like at that time of year.
Overall, it wasn't a satisfactory experience. Most of the restaurants don't serve in the morning or afternoon because they use those hours to sell their timeshares. Honestly, I wouldn't return to this hotel. As I said before, there are better options for the same price.

reviews.author: alejandra bucio
reviews.text:
A beautiful place, but not worth it!
I came for a work meeting, and from the moment I arrived, the air conditioning in the room wasn't working. It rained, and there were leaks everywhere. The staff is the worst; they don't even attend to you, and when they do, they're rude and unpleasant. A place I definitely wouldn't return to or recommend.

reviews.author: LUZ GLENNY CASTRO ORTIZ
reviews.text: Unfortunately, I was robbed inside the hotel (they took the money from my wallet in the room). Some of the money I had was lost, and there was never any response regarding the investigation into the robbery. Although I liked everything else, I wouldn't return because trust and respect are paramount.

reviews.author: Cesar Palomino
reviews.text: THE ROOMS ARE IN VERY BAD CONDITION, THE PHOTOS THEY PUBLISH ARE NOT REAL, THE ELEVATORS DO NOT WORK, THE STAFF IS ELITIST AND RUDE, THEY WERE NEVER ABLE TO GIVE US A RESERVATION TO EAT AT THE RESTAURANT EXCUSING THAT THEY DID NOT HAVE A SYSTEM BUT THERE WERE ALWAYS PEOPLE IN THE RESTAURANT, I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT AT ALL, THE LOBBY STAFF IS VERY RUDE, THAT IS WHY THEY ARE ON STRIKE BECAUSE THEY DO NOT PAY THEM WELL.

reviews.author: mu hak
reviews.text: I've been at this hotel for four days now, but it's awful. My vacation is just wasting time waiting. You wait 30 minutes to get served at breakfast, you wait 30 minutes to book an à la carte meal at the restaurant, there are no sun loungers by the pool or on the beach, and when you ask the staff, they tell you they don't have any more, the hotel doesn't provide any. The hotel room isn't cleaned properly, and the minibar isn't restocked every day. The meals at the restaurants are always the same; it's the same thing every day. The grounds are nice, but the service is too poor. You also have to wait at least 15 minutes for towels because they're always out! We received a very warm welcome from Mr. Angel. The waiters also tried very hard. The cabanas by the pool or on the beach are overpriced; instead, they could have set up sun loungers so everyone has enough space. Not all the dishes in the restaurant are labeled with their exact ingredients, which is very important to me as I want to know what I'm eating!

reviews.author: Yuniesky Aleman
reviews.text: The hotel was awful. The lobby was so hot, the rooms were filthy and neglected, and the buffet was terrible—what can I say? No variety whatsoever. The atmosphere at the pool was terrible—no music, no activities. It seemed like a hotel for senior citizens. Of all the hotels I've visited in Cancun, this has been the worst. Wow, two stars? I think I gave it way too many.

reviews.author: 박은아
reviews.text:
Not recommended for honeymooners looking for an all-inclusive in Cancun... Spend a little more and get a better one. LOL. Cheap is expensive. Old and outdated...
It's all-inclusive, but the restaurants are not welcoming.
The Royal Suite is not welcoming.
The staff is not friendly.
The food quality is poor.
We booked a 3+1 night stay, but we didn't get a refund and were moved back to our previous accommodation.

reviews.author: J E L R
reviews.text:
Old hotel but with a beautiful lobby
Very good service from the staff
Expensive for what it is, ultimately
Located on one of the best stretches of beach in Cancun
Buffet food is bad, as is typical everywhere
The specialty restaurants are quite mediocre.
If you're demanding, don't go to an all-inclusive resort
Drinks are good quality and always well-stocked.
$2,500 USD for three nights, two adults, two children

reviews.author: Márcia Maria Lopes de Andrade
reviews.text: My experience here has been disappointing! The staff isn't courteous, there aren't many drink options! The bars are closed for several hours a day, terrible logistics! A shame!

reviews.author: Arturo Lamadrid
reviews.text: I was there for a week and the concierge service was very bad. Many would say it was excellent, but unfortunately, they don't know how to demand what they offer. They don't offer the fragrances of the pillows. It's just like an information medium. I feel they should be more committed to their work. I really had a lot of problems.

reviews.author: Gabriel Eduardo Garcia Aguilar
reviews.text: The service from the waiters was excellent, the concierge service left a lot to be desired. What I didn't like was that the bathrooms were far from many key points, the shows were average to bad, they don't have a sports bar, due to the pandemic I understand they close early but that takes points away from them, for the omelets they don't have much variety of ingredients and they don't have enough staff to serve you on the beach lounge chairs, honestly I don't think I'll return.

reviews.author: antonio favela
reviews.text: The food is terrible, the Mexican restaurant looks American, and they stop serving alcohol at 10 pm, sending you to a tiny bar for the entire hotel, and they stop serving at 2 am. That's not 24 hours as they promise.

reviews.author: Jezica Sosa
reviews.text: The buffet and the person who served me, Enrique García, were excellent; the service was very attentive and he's a great person. I stayed in room 3421 👍

reviews.author: Leon VR
reviews.text: Very bad experience with the staff; things go missing from the rooms and they don't take responsibility. The food is mediocre, nothing special. I don't recommend it.

reviews.author: Manuel Arriola Barba
reviews.text: Terrible service, leaks, rude staff, tip first, then service. If you get lukewarm water in the shower, you're in luck.

reviews.author: Leymi Cavazos
reviews.text: It was a bittersweet experience, to be honest. The hotel has the facilities to be a 5-star resort, however, our experience was very eventful. We traveled with a group of 12 cousins ​​and everything went wrong. Three of my cousins ​​were trapped in an elevator for 20 minutes, the power went out in our room for an hour and a half... Anyway, I hope they get their act together.

reviews.author: ARACELY SANCHEZ
reviews.text: The hotel is very nice, but the receptionist's service leaves much to be desired. We also found a huge spider in the bathroom. We asked for help, but no one came to assist.

reviews.author: Rafael Almaguer Soto
reviews.text: It was just a day pass and honestly I didn't like it. I only went to the buffet and the pool. The buffet had very little variety of food and you could feel the sand at the bottom of the pool.

reviews.author: Catia Gonzalez
reviews.text: I expected more from this resort. It's very nice, but the buffet is extremely simple compared to others I've seen in Cancun.

reviews.author: guadalupe blanco
reviews.text: The smell from the elevator floor was awful, if you're near the center you have to deal with the noise from the entertainment, the air conditioning is unbearable, sleeping is a luxury, and the service in the restaurants is incredibly slow. I won't be back.

reviews.author: Carlos Ivan Palacios
reviews.text: Bad experience. The hotel has cockroaches, and the rooms are poorly maintained. The service at reception is very poor, not to mention the harassment trying to sell memberships.

reviews.author: Alfredo Valle de la Torre
reviews.text: And I forgot to mention that apart from the late-night music at such a high volume, to top it all off there's construction going on from early in the morning so you can't even sleep 8 hours straight peacefully

reviews.author: Karla Cardenas
reviews.text: It used to be a good hotel, but now it leaves much to be desired in terms of quality, service, and cleanliness.

reviews.author: Maria Manrique
reviews.text: Very poor service from reception staff, bellhops, and especially waiters. The food also leaves much to be desired, and there's constant noise from renovations.

reviews.author: Nuray Yurcel
reviews.text: The hotel was okay, but the service was terrible. Eduardo, the concierge, offered no solutions, and Roberto from security was extremely rude. The event coordinators were incapable of providing service or solutions. I do not recommend this hotel.

reviews.author: Cristian Argotti
reviews.text: This time it wasn't so good, they've removed benefits, but the customer service was magnificent.

reviews.author: BRUNO GUIMARÃES
reviews.text: The facilities are top-notch, but the service is poor and the food is very weak for the price we paid!

reviews.author: Nikoletta Maczkó
reviews.text: The hotels in the hotel zone are all over the place, I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone, we definitely won't be back.

reviews.author: kleber aguiar
reviews.text: Poor service at reception, long lines at check-in, and terrible service in the restaurants and bars!

reviews.author: elizabeth parra
reviews.text: The food was terrible, there was no air conditioning in the nightclub, and there was no atmosphere for young people.

reviews.author: Maria Cristina Cerchiari Fracchetta
reviews.text: Nice, clean place... but the food isn't very good.

reviews.author: Rodrigo Branchini
reviews.text: Be aware that some rooms are very old. I had problems and had to change rooms twice.

reviews.author: Gerardo Javier Gonzalez Cepeda
reviews.text: If you're a foreigner, everything's fine, but if you're Mexican, they discriminate against you and don't even pay attention to you. I'm not coming back.

reviews.author: JONATHAN RODRIGUEZ
reviews.text: The facilities look very old and lack general maintenance.

reviews.author: Juan Carlos Zedillo
reviews.text: Overall, everything was very bad.

reviews.author: Marcelo Elfenbaum

reviews.author: Juan Manuel Albarran
reviews.text: Poor attention from security personnel in the supplier area

reviews.author: Raymundo Mireles
reviews.text: Bad food and uncomfortable spaces

reviews.author: Ana Maria González
reviews.text: The worst one I've ever been to.

reviews.author: laura e
reviews.text: Very bad service

reviews.author: Carlos Hernandez
reviews.text: Evils

reviews.author: Ricardo Gongora Arias
reviews.text: Keep celebrating

reviews.author: Oscar Gutierrez
reviews.text: Terrible service

reviews.author: Luis lauro Gomez saldaña
reviews.text: Excellent place

reviews.author: Rubicel Diaz
reviews.text: The Sal Restaurant was excellent, Horacio at the pool was the best and always attentive, Perla and Alejandro in the cafeteria were always attentive, that's individually but in general the hotel was very disorganized, they don't know how to solve any problems or doubts, and they end up charging extra for things.

reviews.author: Lissete González
reviews.text: The experience of returning after the reopening wasn't very pleasant. The staff was very poorly organized, check-in was slow, the concierge kept ignoring us and didn't know how to handle most of our requests. We understand she's new, but she was never able to resolve any of our issues. It's disappointing because we've been coming to this hotel for many years. Aside from that, the facilities are excellent and the food is as delicious as ever.

reviews.author: Philip Mccleary
reviews.text:
Pascqual and Armando at the buffet were amazing. Very helpful.

Overall the resort has changed. We have been to Paradisus 4 times and this time the overall quality was just average. The food quality and variety was not good. It was the same food every day, salty and bland. We love the staff, but overall we are not happy with the hotel and will not be back.

Outside the hotel we also noticed the people were not as warm, inviting or friendly. It’s not the Cancún we remember and love.

reviews.author: Nophar Haimovitz
reviews.text:
Beautiful hotel. Incredible beach. But everything else? Not great.

We arrived opening week and even though we knew there will be some kinks it was just not a good stay. And since this is not a new hotel I don't think it has anything to do with the reopening.
•	Dinner buffet was empty!! (multiple nights) with a huge line.
•	Almost no food during the day (no fruits and one snack bar)
•	Breakfast okay, lunch mediocre
•	Restaurants are hard to book and very slow in service
•	Zero!!! vegetarian options (I barely ate all stay). I had to beg for veggie food every night. They literally have nothing. And I saw a guy asking for a veggie burger and getting meat because the lady didn't understand).
It's ridiculous that at a hotel in Mexico there are very little unripe fruits (I mean no avocado no mango) no rice and beans. Really low quality food at the buffet.

Service was frustrating:
•	Everything had to be asked for multiple times
•	Drinks were warm (no cold beer or cold champagne)
•	No coffee capsules in the room (they were out)

Our Room issues:
We had a huge leak and while they fixed it (yay strangers in my room during vacation for 2 days) we were offered to move to a smaller, worse rooms instead of a real solution bc "we get what we paid for" (we paid a hefty sum!).

Most concerning:
Our 8-year-old got injured at the kids club and fractured his elbow. We spent a day at the local hospital and No follow-up, no real response from staff. No one cared.

Only reason this isn’t a total 0:
Our concierge Alejandro (and Josmarie) were amazing and genuinely tried to help. Without Alejandro this vacation would have been really bad.

There is potential here, the property is beautiful, the Italian & Asian restaurants are good, and the spa was excellent.

But right now? Would not recommend,  especially for families or vegetarians.

reviews.author: Daniel Bazzo
reviews.text:
I recently stayed at Paradisus Cancun and unfortunately had a pretty disappointing experience overall.

On our last night, we found multiple roaches in the room, which was extremely unsettling. The nightlife also ends at 11pm, which makes it difficult to enjoy a proper evening out.

There are some positives, there are decent amenities for kids, and the upgraded slides were a nice touch. The beach itself is beautiful, but seating is very limited. There are not nearly enough umbrellas, which is a big issue when you have kids who can’t stay in the sun all day.

The resort is still under construction, which really takes away from the experience. On top of that, there were two conventions happening during our stay, making it nearly impossible to book reservations. It felt like everything enjoyable required extra money or becoming a member.

We were especially disappointed that we couldn’t enjoy a proper steak dinner as a family because kids aren’t allowed at certain restaurants. For a family resort, that doesn’t make much sense.

There were also safety concerns, tiles in the main pool were broken, and someone actually cut their foot. For a hotel that recently went through renovations, the quality of work seems questionable.

Management was another issue. We had reservations for 15 people at Kow Restaurant for my mom’s 70th birthday, but they split our group up. The same thing happened at the Italian restaurant, where they initially couldn’t accommodate us even though it was empty. After some back and forth, the manager Daniel stepped in and allowed 8 of us to sit at separate tables. He did make an effort by bringing out a surprise cake once he learned about the birthday, which we appreciated, but only 4 of us were actually able to share that moment together.

The staff overall were friendly and constantly asked for reviews, and while they do deserve recognition for their effort, it doesn’t reflect the overall condition and management of the hotel.

Vianney was absolutely incredible. We came in having a pretty rough day, and she completely turned the experience around for us. From the moment she greeted us, she was warm, attentive, and genuinely caring. She went above and beyond to make sure everything was perfect, and her positive energy made a huge difference.

Balthazar also did a great job. He was attentive, professional, and made sure everything ran smoothly throughout our visit.

It’s rare to come across a team that can shift your entire mood like that, but they did just that. Outstanding service and an even better attitude, they truly made our day. We’ll definitely be back because of them.

Between being understaffed, poorly executed renovations, and constant limitations unless you pay extra, I would not recommend this resort unless you’re okay eating buffet food daily and spending more for basic experiences.

reviews.author: Peter Williams
reviews.text:
Miguel is an awesome waiter and Lemon Fish is a beautiful restaurant with lovely food. Small portions but very delicious. Need to know what to order here.

The other restaurants also have some issues and I will write a longer review of the whole hotel after leaving. It is being renovated in June and not a moment too soon!

reviews.author: Julia Blazejewski
reviews.text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here for 4 nights in early March 2025. After reading many five star reviews prior to arriving, we were surprised to realize that our stay did not match other guests’ experiences.

The room we received was in definite need of an upgrade; the bathroom was pretty run down, and the couch in the room had stains on it. We were not expecting a fancy room by any means because we knew we booked the most basic option. However, we were still expecting the room to be in good condition. Also, when booking, I was told I would receive a $200 credit to be used for a room upgrade. When we arrived, we found out only $50 of the $200 could be used for a room upgrade, which was not nearly enough. I had called the resort a couple months prior to clarify the credit, and even then, no one had informed me of the full terms of the credit. This felt very misleading.

We didn’t have any issues getting reservations at the restaurants, but the food was not good and not up to par with what should be served at a four-star resort. The service was not that great either. Some of the servers came off as slightly rude, and nobody really checked up on us. At Lemon Fish, we waited almost an hour for our server to take our order and bring our meal out. We also did not appreciate that the servers occasionally tried to up charge us by trying to sell the food and drink upgrade options, but not telling us they would cost extra unless we explicitly asked. The food at the buffet was alright, and was honestly a better option for dinner than the restaurants. The dessert options were bad; the ice cream by the pool was delicious though and one of the highlights of the resort. The drinks were good, but watered down which is to be expected at an all inclusive. The best drinks were at Ginger bar.

The resort is beautiful, and the beach and pools are perfect. I recommend waking up at 7-8 am to claim seating by the pool or beach, as it fills up pretty quickly. The resort also had nightly entertainment, which was nice.

All in all, if food and service are important factors for you, I would recommend staying elsewhere. I imagine that booking at The Reserve could make it a little more worthwhile though.

reviews.author: Sam Michlig
reviews.text:
The hotel is saved by it's fantastic hard working restaurant and bar staff. Every morning for breakfast (and often lunch) we relaxed on the outdoor terrace at the Buffet restaurant and were looked after by Alberto and Joni who were an absolute pleasure to talk to and excellent hosts. Thank you also to them from our 2 young children who were treated just as well as the grown ups.

We also enjoyed Aqua Marina where we were looked after by Erick, Wilbert and Sergio during the lunch service and Roberto in the evening.

Jesus at Capello, Melvin at Cielo and Daniel at Lemon Fish also are fantastic waiters.

For the people above, and for many more incredibly hard working staff around the pool and beach - they are working at 5 star standard all day long. Management need to look to themselves for areas that are making global review scores lower - and take the pressure off their employees.

The issue here at management level is greed. On the run up to the stay there was frequent contact from concierge services but only with a view to selling room upgrades or experience packages. Simple requests like a room on a higher floor or in a quieter area were squarely ignored once it was clear that no further cash could be extracted.

Fending off regular approaches from the 'circle club' sales team to attend seminars - not what I want to do on holiday. Some staff are clearly under pressure to sell upgrades for wine or 'chefs specials' and the daily rounds from the Spa and watersports excursions team. It can all lead to the need to say no thank you 10 times a day and walk around not making eye contact to avoid sales approaches.

The big problem with our stay was the room we were allocated on the first night. It was actively dirty with blood on the vanity worktop. Light switches were cracked, lamps didn't work and I killed 5 cockroaches in the bathroom. It was an extremely unpleasant environment and to top it all - incredibly noisy. This room was in dire need of renovation and shouldn't be in use currently for paying guests.

The response from reception was very disinterested - they processed a room change request which required me to return to reception at 0900 and again at 1500 to move room. Very disruptive to the holiday and absolutely zero concern about the state of the room. The reception team even suggested the next room might be in the same condition so there was no point moving. No apology was ever offered either.

The complaints process was dissatisfactory and I have since received a refund via my credit card company for the night spent in a dirty room. The hotel refused to refund but offered an upgrade voucher for a future stay which i declined.

The hotel itself occupies a huge amount of beach front and as a result has stunning views from all around the pool areas and lots of the dining and drinking areas. The building is old but there is a constant effort being made to maintain improve and re-paint areas. The food was excellent. Drinks selection also fantastic and the bar tenders in the mixology bar made incredible cocktails. Kanna Beach Bar is the perfect spot for the final drink before getting ready for the evening.

reviews.author: Mrs. Muñoz
reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed here for 5 nights. We loved the hotel and location. The decor and atmosphere is beautiful. The view of the beach is breathtaking.

The service unfortunately is not up to par and this is what didn’t make it the best experience we were hoping for.

Alondra who checked us in at The Reserve was very matter of fact, rude, and unwelcoming.  She didn’t welcome us with a smile when we arrived and didn’t even ask about our experience when we checked out. It was very revealing of her character and lack of professionalism.

Some of the employees who work at the other restaurants and buffets can also be very disrespectful with their actions and lack of professionalism. There was an employee who worked in the kitchen at the Malva Buffet who ignored me and rolled her eyes when I kindly asked where the omelets were being served, and had a bad attitude when I asked to speak to the person in charge about her actions.

On a positive note, I do have to say Gerardo who works as a server at the Malva buffet is very kind-hearted and cares about making your experience memorable. He went out of his way to always make sure we were cared for. Fernando at Blue Agave also stood out from the rest with his heart of service. Ismael at the spa was also patient and kind with us.

There are some kind employees there~ but it’s honestly a hit or miss.

They need to be consistent with their service and I hope they take this review as an eye opener to coach their employees  about the seriousness and importance of quality customer service.

reviews.author: Shanell Spann
reviews.text: Probably wouldn't choose this hotel again as there was a lot of wear/tear, but the grounds are wonderful for photos

reviews.author: Laura Hudson
reviews.text:
We purchased ocean view room and was given a room on the 0 floor that had no view. The air conditioning sounded like a jack hammer and the shower drain smelled horrible. We asked for a new room and was given one the next day on the 3rd floor. View was incredible. The next issue was we were above the lounge area so there was music bumping until 11pm.
Long wait lines checking in.
Room service food was always cold.
Food and service at the pool were the best.
Staff very friendly.
Beach was great.
Our last night they had some kind of sewer break or leak in the buffet area. They tried to stop it and clean but kept bringing people in to eat and the smell was horrible.
We will not go back.

reviews.author: mahtab ghafoorian
reviews.text:
I recently stayed at paradisus Cancún and overall had a nice time, but I was very disappointed with how a check-out situation was handled, especially considering the level of service I expected.

My flight was early, so we checked out at 6:15 AM, well before the official 12:30 PM check-out time. Breakfast was supposed to be served at 6:30 AM, and I kindly asked if we could enter the buffet 10 minutes earlier, just to grab something quickly before heading to the airport. The staff member (Henry) refused, which I understand might be policy — but what upset me was the dismissive attitude and the lack of willingness to even hear our situation.

Worse, after we checked out and our bracelets were cut (which the front desk said was fine), we kept our bracelets in our pocket, as we were still within our valid check-out time. Henry said we couldn’t access the breakfast buffet without a bracelet and would have to pay extra — even though we were still entitled to full service. When I explained this, he refused to speak respectfully or offer any help. I ended up going to reception to report the incident and ask for the manager’s contact.

The 24-hour Nespresso bar is a nice touch, but the pastries weren’t great, which is why I wanted a proper breakfast. I truly expected better customer service — especially in how staff communicate with guests in a rush or under stress.

It’s really a shame because, before this situation, I was very pleased with the resort and had a great experience overall. Unfortunately, the poor interaction with staff (Henry) has made me reconsider recommending this resort or returning again.

reviews.author: Paul Peterson
reviews.text:
The service was not good. Lines for food, for reservations. Room service tacos were terrible. You have to get your beer and bring them to the room. The restaurants meals were not good. There are not enough shaded areas around the pool. If you did not get a chair by pool by 8 am you are not getting one later. Our package included transportation from airport was not available so we were out $300 to make arrangements at the airport. We tried to upgrade to the adult side the reserve but no vacancies. The noi
se from the loud music outside and the noise inside the lobby area made it impossible to have a quiet rest. I could go on and on, by far our worst experience. The entire time I was washing we could check out and got  to Aqua Live.

reviews.author: Anthony Dinse
reviews.text:
The location is convenient especially with the aqua world directly across the road for some activities. The resort is beautiful in general especially the main lobby area. The service was usually pretty good with friendly wait staff across the resort. The food at most restaurants is average at best with little flavor. As many other posts noted you can probably stick to the buffet each day and have the same or better experience. The room was showing signs of its age. Fridge was broken and when they “fixed” it, while now cold it started making loud noises. I will say they acted promptly when it was brought to their attention. Most frustrating part of the stay as other also mention is the pool/beach seating situation. They allow other guests to place 4,5,6…etc towels on all the chairs in large sections at 6:30-7am. Those guests then sometimes don’t arrive to the pool/beach until 3-4 hours later since they “claimed” these seats. If you show up after 8am good luck finding a spot anywhere. And typically once they leave half the time they leave their towel instead of placing it in the bins so 80% of the chairs appear taken when someone left hours ago… pretty crazy situation every single day. Seems like a simple fix, but from other reviews they refuse to address it so it continues…
The service was spotty as well. On average someone would come by once a hour to ask for drink orders… sometimes more sometimes less. lovely resort and people but probably wouldn’t return due to the just ok food and the terrible pool/beach seating.

reviews.author: Elaina Prakash
reviews.text: Service review : Fantastic. The service of the reserve staff - Gabriela, Miguel, Luis and Victor at the Reserve was impeccable. Gabriela and Miguel, specifically went out of their way to make us comfortable at the Reserve pool. They were incredibly attentive and genuinely happy to be helping us. We didn’t even have to ask for drink refills. They were so attentive and made our time at the pool very fun and relaxing.

reviews.author: Ramiyan Sujeeve
reviews.text: The resort was alright... The view and pools were great, but the beach was off-limits (seaweed). Rooms were alright but renovations are needed. Overall a pretty solid resort.

reviews.author: Salena Navarez
reviews.text: Edgar in Capella restaurant was amazing. Best service the whole trip

reviews.author: Tim Rolfe
reviews.text:
This is a review of the Fahrenheit pool
Bar only, where Roberto and Juan Manuel are absolutely excellent. Really quick and attentive service. They represent only very few of the staff members that actually understand service. I would hire them!  Fuller review of hotel and experience to follow….

reviews.author: Vanessa Huang
reviews.text:
I spent 7 days in this resort and want to share my honest opinion.

Starting off with pros:
- We got a crib for our 1.5 year old in our room on the day we arrived with no extra charge
- The staff, especially the servers are kind, enthusiastic and accommodating. The servers in the restaurant were super accommodating and made special meals for my 1.5 year old, which I appreciate so much.
- The entire resort is very clean and pretty
- There is a kids club where you can drop off your kids and they have activities to keep them entertained

Cons:
- We found out that the corn in the buffet was spoiled a couple times
- The are 2 main elevators for the 8-story building and one elevator didn’t work half the time and the other one is extremely slow
- The room is dark and outdated - the door in bathroom doesn’t close, the toilet doesn’t flush properly
- There’s leaks in the hallway ceilings here and there

Overall we had a great time but the quality of the building is not good.

reviews.author: Jason hanley
reviews.text: Beautiful ocean views and pools, our only 2 complaints were (1) food/drinks, plan on spending more for upgraded meals and drinks, all 45 people in our party would agree. (2) our concierge for the reserve side didn’t share the free things we get but have to book, daily pool cabana or hydrotherapy session at spa (spa was fabulous!)

reviews.author: Jimmie Estrada
reviews.text:
This hotel is absolutely gorgeous. The beach and pools are clean and nice and the service is mostly great. We had an issue with the shower and they sent someone up to fix it immediately.

My biggest complaint though was the food. The buffet was pretty bad. I’ve had better hospital food. The restaurants are very hit or miss. I really enjoyed Blue Agave but Capella was just okay and the place by the pool was probably one of the weirdest meals I’ve eaten at a restaurant. The sea bass was burnt and the mussels had some kind of Alfredo sauce drizzled on the shells.

Our room was pretty dated and the bed skirts had weird stains. One of the box springs was ripped and you could see it hanging down under the bed skirt. The bedding was not what I’d expect even for a 4 star hotel. Lumpy pillows/not plush mattress/sheets were standard threadcount.

I also had a weird interaction with a guest services staff member who misheard me when I told him my room number and then argued with me and said I gave him the wrong room number. He was not friendly and also gave me wrong information about my shuttle back to the airport and told me I’d have to pay for it and book it through one of the excursion desks in the lobby. Talked to someone else and it turns out that wasn’t true. The restaurant staff, bellhops, and housekeeping were very nice though.

I’d consider staying here again if the food was better but more than likely I’ll try somewhere else in the future.

reviews.author: Brigitte Gravelle
reviews.text:
The resort is beautiful and has a lot of potential. Food was great! Cabella was our favourite and Francisco and Dayvison were amazing servers!!!

If only all the other departments were as well staffed. The beach and pool areas were understaffed and lounge chairs were not available unless you went out before 6 am. There was 1 person for the entire resort for dinner reservations which led to having to wait in line for over 1.5 hrs only to be told nothing was available and we could only make reservations for 3 days at a time. We asked for a bottle opener on the first day we were here and never received it, and the bar fridge was not consistently restocked. The rooms are very dated.

reviews.author: Corina Settles
reviews.text:
This was our second time returning to Paradisus since our first time experience staying here was wonderful.

The room during our recent stay was not enjoyable, the air conditioning was not cool enough at night requiring us to request multiple times someone to assess the air conditioning. After multiple attempts, we were accompanied with a plug-in fan on the 2nd to last night that  helped with the room temperature enough.  The lighting function of the room was not up to par. The entry, living room and overhead bathroom sink lights were not working.

Roberto from the pool area was a wonderful service person and truly accommodated our requests as best possible every day during our stay. He is an extremely hard worker and would honestly return just for the sake of his service. Irina from the guest services bar was also very lovely, also Juan Manuel at the pool bar was excellent.

This resort is less than 20 minutes from the airport and they offer a taxi service to the airport for about $42 if needed.

reviews.author: Becky Cunning
reviews.text:
This was our second trip to Paradisus, the first trip being six years ago.  We have highly recommended this resort to many friends and family over the years.  However, this year was disappointing - not everything but enough that those are the things you remember.
First - Victor who is the pool concierge is AMAZING!!  5+ stars for Victor alone.  He is helpful, kind, fun, and goes above and beyond!  We enjoyed working and visiting with him.
Moises and Javier at the pool always took good care of us without any hesitation - they get five stars as well.
Our hotel concierge, Lily, was hardly seen and certainly didn't go out of her to make things easy as a five star hotel should.  Her sending us the activity list for the day at 3:00pm served no purpose at that point of the day.  We saw many others coming out and checking on their guest.  In our party of five, I personally saw her one time. Lily does not get five stars.
The pool was usually dirty, or dirtier than it should have been.  We were in the adult only pool, so should see a little less filth, than that of sharing with multiple families.  We saw them cleaning the pool, but would never keep the water above the skimmers in order for the pool itself to keep up with some of the problems.  This was in the adult pool and in the small "tanning pool".
The rooms were very disappointing, enough so that we moved room once and still wanted to a second time.
The air conditioning was not working well at all, in either room.
It was already not working well and then when housekeeping or turn down service would come in, they would turn the air conditioning OFF.  We would come back in at night ready for bed and have to deal with a hot room.  I was not happy about that.
